title.zh: 卷六十六 列傳第三十六 劉弘 陶侃
title.en: Volume 66 Biographies 36: Liu Hong; Tao Kan
title.raw: 卷六十六 列傳第三十六 劉弘 陶侃 Volume 66 Biographies 36: Liu Hong; Tao Kan

sentences.zh: 劉弘，字和季，沛國相人也。

translations.literal: Liu Hong, courtesy name Heji, was a man of Xiang in the state of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong, whose courtesy name was Heji, came from Xiang in the kingdom of Pei.

sentences.zh: 祖馥，魏揚州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fu was Inspector of Yang province under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Liu Fu had served the state of Wei as regional inspector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 父靖，鎮北將軍。

translations.literal: His father Jing was General Who Guards the North.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Liu Jing, held the rank of general who guards the north.

sentences.zh: 弘有幹略政事之才，少家洛陽，與武帝同居永安裏，又同年，共研席。

translations.literal: Hong had talent for capacity, strategy, and handling government affairs; in youth his family was in Luoyang, and he dwelt together with Emperor Wu in Yong'an ward, was also the same year of birth, and shared the same study mat.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong had a gift for administration and strategic leadership. While still young he lived in Luoyang in the same lane as the future Emperor Wu—Yong'an ward—and, born the same year, they studied together as close companions.

sentences.zh: 以舊恩起家太子門大夫，累遷率更令，轉太宰長史。

translations.literal: By old favor he rose from family status to become Gentleman at the Gate of the Heir Apparent, was promoted in stages to Director of the Clepsydra, and transferred to be senior clerk to the grand tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to that long-standing connection he first entered office as gentleman at the heir apparent's gate, then rose through the directorate for the heir's clepsydra office before becoming chief clerk to the grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 張華甚重之。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua thought very highly of him.

sentences.zh: 由是為甯朔將軍、假節、監幽州諸軍事，領烏丸校尉，甚有威惠，寇盜屏跡，為幽朔所稱。

translations.literal: Thereupon he became General Who Pacifies the North, with credential staff, supervised military affairs of You province, and concurrently held Colonel of the Wuhuan; he had very much awe and kindness, bandits and robbers withdrew their tracks, and he was praised by You and the northern region.
translations.idiomatic: On that basis he was appointed general who pacifies the north, given a credential staff, and charged with supervising all military affairs in Youzhou while also serving as colonel of the Wuhuan. His blend of firm authority and generous rule cleared the roads of raiders, and the north praised his governance.

sentences.zh: 以勳德兼茂，封宣城公。

translations.literal: By meritorious service and virtue both luxuriant, he was enfeoffed as duke of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: For outstanding merit and moral stature he was invested as duke of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 太安中，張昌作亂，轉使持節、南蠻校尉、荊州刺史，率前將軍趙驤等討昌，自方城至宛、新野，所向皆平。

translations.literal: In the Tai'an era, Zhang Chang raised rebellion; Hong was transferred to bearer of the staff of authority, Colonel of the Southern Man, and Inspector of Jing province, and led Forward General Zhao Xiang and others to attack Chang; from Fangcheng to Wan and Xinyang, wherever he went all was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tai'an years Zhang Chang rose in revolt. Liu Hong was reassigned as commissioner with full authority, colonel of the southern tribes, and inspector of Jingzhou, and he marched with Forward General Zhao Xiang and others against Zhang Chang. From Fangcheng south to Wan and Xinye, every objective he struck was brought to heel.

sentences.zh: 及新野王歆之敗也，以弘代為鎮南將軍、都督荊州諸軍事，餘官如故。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Xinye Xin was defeated, by Hong in his place as General Who Guards the South and area commander for all military affairs of Jing province, the remaining offices as before.
translations.idiomatic: After Prince Sima Xin of Xinye met defeat, Liu Hong succeeded him as general who guards the south and area commander over all Jingzhou forces, while keeping his other titles unchanged.

sentences.zh: 弘遣南蠻長史陶侃為大都護，參軍蒯恆為義軍督護，牙門將皮初為都戰帥，進據襄陽。

translations.literal: Hong sent Southern Man senior clerk Tao Kan as grand protector, adjutant Kuai Heng as protector of the righteous army, and camp-gate general Pi Chu as chief battle commander, advancing to occupy Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong appointed his chief clerk for the southern tribes, Tao Kan, as grand protector of the army; his adjutant Kuai Heng as commander of the volunteer corps; and the camp-gate officer Pi Chu as chief field commander. They advanced and secured Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 張昌並軍圍宛，敗趙驤軍，弘退屯梁。

translations.literal: Zhang Chang combined armies and besieged Wan, defeated Zhao Xiang's army, and Hong retreated to garrison Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang concentrated his forces and invested Wan, routed Zhao Xiang's command, and forced Liu Hong to pull back and encamp at Liang.

sentences.zh: 侃、初等累戰破昌，前後斬首數萬級。

translations.literal: Kan, Chu, and others repeatedly battled and defeated Chang; before and after they beheaded several tens of thousands of grades.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan, Pi Chu, and their men fought Zhang Chang again and again, cutting off tens of thousands of heads in the course of the campaign.

sentences.zh: 及到官，昌懼而逃，其眾悉降，荊土平。

translations.literal: When he arrived at office, Chang feared and fled, his masses all surrendered, and the land of Jing was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Liu Hong reached his post, Zhang Chang had fled in panic and his followers had all capitulated, and peace returned to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，弘之退也，范陽王虓遣長水校尉張奕領荊州。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Hong had retreated, the Prince of Fanyang Xiu had sent Colonel of the Long River Zhang Yi to take charge of Jing province.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during Liu Hong's retreat, Prince Sima Xiu of Fanyang had already ordered Colonel Zhang Yi of the long-shore guard to take over Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 弘至，奕不受代，與兵距弘。

translations.literal: When Hong arrived, Yi did not accept replacement, and with soldiers resisted Hong.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Hong arrived, Zhang Yi refused to hand over command and opposed him with armed force.

sentences.zh: 弘遣軍討奕，斬之，表曰：「臣以凡才，謬荷國恩，作司方州，奉辭伐罪，不能奮揚雷霆，折沖萬里，軍退于宛，分受顯戮。

translations.literal: Hong sent troops to attack Yi, beheaded him, and memorialized saying: 'Your subject by ordinary talent wrongly bears the state's grace, acts as steward of a regional province, received orders to attack guilt, was unable to rouse and display thunder, to repel conflict at ten thousand li, the army retreated at Wan, and in part ought to receive manifest execution.'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong sent troops against Zhang Yi, executed him, and submitted a memorial: "I am a man of middling ability who has nonetheless been showered with imperial favor and entrusted with a great province. Ordered to punish the guilty, I failed to strike like thunder or to shield the realm from harm a thousand miles away; my army fell back at Wan, and I deserve the heaviest punishment for that failure."

sentences.zh: 猥蒙含宥，被遣之職，即進達所鎮。

translations.literal: Vulgarly receiving inclusion and forgiveness, was dispatched to the duty, immediately advanced and reached the place garrisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty bore with me and, instead of punishment, sent me back to my post; I pressed on at once to the headquarters I hold.

sentences.zh: 而范陽王虓先遣前長水校尉張奕領荊州，臣至，不受節度，擅舉兵距臣。

translations.literal: But the Prince of Fanyang Xiu had first sent former Colonel of the Long River Zhang Yi to take charge of Jing province; when your subject arrived, he did not accept regulation, on his own authority raised troops and resisted your subject.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Prince Sima Xiu of Fanyang had already put the former colonel of the long-shore guard, Zhang Yi, in charge of Jingzhou. When I arrived, Zhang Yi refused my orders, raised troops on his own authority, and resisted me.

sentences.zh: 今張昌奸党初平，昌未梟擒，益梁流人蕭條猥集，無賴之徒易相扇動，飆風駭蕩，則滄海橫波，苟患失之，無所不至，比須表上，慮失事機，輒遣軍討奕，即梟其首。

translations.literal: Now Zhang Chang's wicked faction is first pacified, Chang is not yet hung captured, Yi and Liang displaced persons desolate and vulgarly gather, roving good-for-nothings easily mutually fan and move, whirlwind wind frightens and tosses, then the deep sea crosses waves; if one grasps fear of losing, there is nothing to which they will not go; comparing must memorialize upward, fearing to lose the opportunity of affairs, then sent troops to attack Yi, immediately hung his head.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang's confederates have only just been subdued, and Zhang Chang himself is still at large. Refugees from Yizhou and Liangzhou are pouring in, destitute and packed together, easy prey for any adventurer who stirs them up. One gust of rumor and the whole region could surge like a storm at sea. If men panic for their own safety, they will stop at nothing. Waiting for a memorial to reach the capital might cost us the critical moment, so I sent troops against Zhang Yi and had his head displayed at once.

sentences.zh: 奕雖貪亂，欲為荼毒，由臣劣弱，不勝其任，令奕肆心，以勞資斧，敢引覆餗之刑，甘受專輒之罪。

translations.literal: Although Yi was greedy for chaos, wished to be bitter poison, it was because your subject was inferior and weak, could not bear the duty, caused Yi to give free rein to his heart, thereby toiling the executioner's axe; dares to cite the punishment of overturning the cauldron, willingly receives the crime of acting on one's own authority.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi may have been greedy for turmoil and eager to do harm, but the deeper fault is mine: I was too weak for the task and let him run wild until the axe had to fall. I accept the disgrace of incompetence and the charge of having exceeded my authority without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「將軍文武兼資，前委方夏，宛城不守，咎由趙驤。

translations.literal: An edict said: 'The general combines civil and martial endowment; formerly was entrusted with the great summer region; Wan city was not guarded; the fault lies with Zhao Xiang.'
translations.idiomatic: The court replied: "You are a commander equally at home with brush and sword. When the southern heartland was entrusted to you, the loss of Wan lay with Zhao Xiang, not with your leadership."

sentences.zh: 將軍所遣諸軍，克滅群寇，張奕貪禍，距違詔命。

translations.literal: The various armies the general sent were able to destroy the mass of bandits; Zhang Yi was greedy for disaster, resisted and violated edict orders.
translations.idiomatic: The forces you dispatched crushed the rebels. Zhang Yi courted disaster by defying an imperial mandate.

sentences.zh: 將軍致討，傳首闕庭，雖有不請之嫌，古人有專之之義。

translations.literal: The general carried out punishment, transmitted the head to the palace courtyard; although there is the suspicion of not requesting, the ancients had the righteousness of acting with sole authority.
translations.idiomatic: You moved against him and sent his head to the capital. Even if that skipped prior approval, the classics recognize occasions when a field commander must act on his own.

sentences.zh: 其恢宏奧略，鎮綏南海，以副推轂之望焉。

translations.literal: Expand grand profound strategy, pacify and soothe the southern sea, thereby to match the expectation of pushing the wheel hub.'
translations.idiomatic: Continue to unfold your grand design and steady the southern lands, so that the court's confidence in you—like the general whose chariot the ruler himself pushes—is fully justified.

sentences.zh: 」張昌竄於下雋山，弘遣軍討昌，斬之，悉降其眾。

translations.literal: Zhang Chang fled to Xiachun mountain; Hong sent troops to attack Chang, beheaded him, and all his masses surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang fled into the hills at Xiachun. Liu Hong sent troops after him, took his life, and accepted the surrender of his entire army.

sentences.zh: 時荊部守宰多闕，弘請補選，帝從之。

translations.literal: At that time in the Jing region many prefects and chiefs were lacking; Hong requested to supplement selection, and the emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Many county and commandery posts in Jingzhou stood vacant. Liu Hong asked permission to fill them, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 弘乃敘功銓德，隨才補授，甚為論者所稱。

translations.literal: Hong then arranged merit and weighed virtue, according to talent supplemented and appointed, and was greatly praised by those who discussed.
translations.idiomatic: He ranked candidates by merit and character and appointed each to a post suited to his abilities, which earned wide praise among contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 乃表曰：「被中詔，敕臣隨資品選，補諸缺吏。

translations.literal: Then he memorialized saying: 'Received the inner edict, ordered your subject according to rank and grade to select, to supplement the various lacking officials.'
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial: "I have received an edict from the palace instructing me to appoint officials to vacant posts strictly according to rank and seniority."

sentences.zh: 夫慶賞刑威，非臣所專，且知人則哲，聖帝所難，非臣暗蔽所能斟酌。

translations.literal: As for reward celebration and punishment awe, these are not what your subject monopolizes; moreover knowing people then wise, what even a sage emperor finds difficult, is not what your subject's dim obstruction can weigh and pour.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards, punishments, and the awe they inspire are not mine to monopolize. Even a sage finds it hard to read men truly; a dull provincial governor like myself can hardly pretend to judge every case perfectly.

sentences.zh: 然萬事有機，豪厘宜慎，謹奉詔書，差所應用。

translations.literal: Yet the myriad affairs have their pivot points; a hair's breadth ought to be cautious; respectfully received the edict document, differentiated what ought to be applied.
translations.idiomatic: Yet every decision turns on fine points where a hair's breadth matters. I have therefore obeyed the edict to the letter while weighing each appointment with care.

sentences.zh: 蓋崇化莫若貴德，則所以濟屯，故太上立德，其次立功也。

translations.literal: For promoting transformation nothing compares to honoring virtue; then that by which to aid difficulty; therefore the highest establishes virtue, next establishes merit.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing advances moral order like honoring genuine worth, especially in troubled times. The ancients ranked establishing virtue above establishing mere achievement, and I have tried to follow that scale.

sentences.zh: 頃者多難，淳樸彌凋，臣輒以征士伍朝補零陵太守，庶以懲波蕩之弊，養退讓之操。

translations.literal: Recently there have been many difficulties, simplicity and plainness increasingly withered; your subject then by summoned gentleman Wu Chao supplemented as prefect of Lingling, hoping thereby to punish the harms of wave-tossing turmoil, to nurture the conduct of yielding and yielding.
translations.idiomatic: These years of disaster have eroded simple honesty. I have therefore appointed the recluse-scholar Wu Chao prefect of Lingling, hoping to curb reckless ambition and to foster a climate of modest restraint.

sentences.zh: 臣以不武，前退于宛，長史陶侃、參軍蒯恆、牙門皮初，戮力致討，蕩滅奸凶，侃恆各以始終軍事，初為都戰帥，忠勇冠軍，漢沔清肅，實初等之勳也。

translations.literal: Your subject by lack of martial ability, formerly retreated at Wan; senior clerk Tao Kan, adjutant Kuai Heng, camp-gate Pi Chu, joined strength to carry out punishment, swept away and destroyed wicked fierce; Kan and Heng each by beginning-to-end military affairs, Chu as chief battle commander, loyalty and courage crowned the army, Han and Mian were cleared and solemn; truly it is the merit of Chu and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Though I myself lacked military brilliance and once fell back at Wan, my chief clerk Tao Kan, adjutant Kuai Heng, and camp officer Pi Chu threw themselves into the campaign, rooted out the traitors, and restored order along the Han and Mian rivers. Tao Kan and Kuai Heng saw the operation through from start to finish; Pi Chu led the van with conspicuous loyalty and courage. The peace we now enjoy on that front is largely their doing.

sentences.zh: 《司馬法》'賞不逾時'，欲人知為善之速福也。

translations.literal: The Methods of Sima: 'Rewards do not exceed the time,' desiring people to know the speedy fortune of doing good.
translations.idiomatic: The Methods of the Marshal says, 'Rewards must not be delayed,' so that men see how quickly virtue brings its reward.

sentences.zh: 若不超報，無以勸徇功之士，慰熊羆之志。

translations.literal: If not surpassingly rewarded, there is no means to encourage those who follow merit, to console the will of bears and brown bears.
translations.idiomatic: Unless such men are rewarded promptly and generously, there is no way to encourage those who risk everything for the realm or to satisfy the zeal of our fiercest fighters.

sentences.zh: 臣以初補襄陽太守，侃為府行司馬，使典論功事，恆為山都令。

translations.literal: Your subject by Chu supplemented as prefect of Xiangyang, Kan as acting marshal of the headquarters, causing to manage discussing merit affairs, Heng as magistrate of Shandu.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore propose Pi Chu as prefect of Xiangyang, Tao Kan as acting marshal of my staff with responsibility for recording battle honors, and Kuai Heng as magistrate of Shandu.

sentences.zh: 詔惟令臣以散補空缺，然沶鄉令虞潭忠誠烈正，首唱義舉，舉善以教，不能者勸，臣輒特轉潭補醴陵令。

translations.literal: The edict only ordered your subject by miscellaneous to supplement vacant posts, yet Shen district magistrate Yu Tan was loyal, sincere, fierce, upright, first raised the righteous undertaking, raised the good thereby to teach, those unable were encouraged; your subject then specially transferred Tan to supplement as magistrate of Liling.
translations.idiomatic: The edict limits me to filling vacancies with men of miscellaneous rank, yet Yu Tan, magistrate of Cen Township, showed blazing loyalty when he first rallied the loyalist cause. His example lifts the worthy and shames the slothful. I have therefore taken the liberty of promoting him to magistrate of Liling.

sentences.zh: 南郡廉吏仇勃，母老疾困，賊至守衛不移，以致拷掠，幾至隕命。

translations.literal: Nan commandery incorrupt official Qiu Bo, mother old illness distressed, when bandits arrived guarded and defended without moving, thereby underwent beating and flogging, almost reached falling life.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Bo, an honest clerk in Nan commandery, refused to abandon his post when raiders came even though his aged mother lay gravely ill at home. They tortured him until he nearly died for that steadfastness.

sentences.zh: 尚書令史郭貞，張昌以為尚書郎，欲訪以朝議，遁逃不出，昌質其妻子，避之彌遠。

translations.literal: Secretariat document clerk Guo Zhen, Zhang Chang by him made Secretariat gentleman, wished to consult him on court deliberations; he fled and hid and did not emerge; Chang held hostage his wife and children; he avoided them ever farther.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhen, a clerk in the secretariat, was named a secretary-cavalier by Zhang Chang, who wanted his advice on state policy. Guo went into hiding and never appeared, so Zhang seized his family as hostages—yet Guo only withdrew further into concealment.

sentences.zh: 勃孝篤著於臨危，貞忠厲於強暴，雖各四品，皆可以訓獎臣子，長益風教。

translations.literal: Bo's filial devotion was manifest at facing peril; Zhen's loyalty was severe toward violent force; although each was fourth rank, all can be used to instruct and encourage ministers and sons, to lengthen and increase wind and teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Bo displayed filial devotion under the gravest danger; Guo Zhen proved his loyalty in the teeth of brute force. Though both men held only middling rank, their conduct is exactly what should be held up to instruct officials and strengthen public morals.

sentences.zh: 臣輒以勃為歸鄉令，貞為信陵令。

translations.literal: Your subject then by Bo as Guixiang magistrate, Zhen as Xinling magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore nominate Qiu Bo as magistrate of Guixiang and Guo Zhen as magistrate of Xinling.

sentences.zh: 皆功行相參，循名校實，條列行狀，公文具上。

translations.literal: All merit and conduct mutually reference, following name examining reality, itemized listed conduct conditions, public documents complete upward.
translations.idiomatic: In every case merit matches conduct; I have checked reputation against fact, drawn up detailed service records, and prepared the full documentary packet for the ministry.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷以初雖有功，襄陽又是名郡，名器宜慎，不可授初，乃以前東平太守夏侯陟為襄陽太守，余並從之。

translations.literal: The court took that although Chu had merit, Xiangyang was also a famous commandery, famous vessels ought to be cautious, could not be given to Chu; then by former Dongping prefect Xiahou Zhi as Xiangyang prefect, the rest all followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The court conceded that Pi Chu had earned distinction but argued that Xiangyang, a premier commandery, was too important an appointment to entrust to him. It named Xiahou Zhi, the former prefect of Dongping, as prefect of Xiangyang instead, while approving Liu Hong's other recommendations.

sentences.zh: 陟，弘之婿也。

translations.literal: Zhi was Hong's son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Zhi was Liu Hong's own son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 弘下教曰：「夫統天下者，宜與天下一心；

translations.literal: Hong issued instruction saying: 'He who governs the realm ought to be of one heart with the realm;'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong issued a directive: "Whoever would rule the empire must stand with the whole empire as one mind."

sentences.zh: 化一國者，宜與一國為任。

translations.literal: He who transforms one state ought to take responsibility together with one state.'
translations.idiomatic: Whoever would transform a single kingdom must shoulder that kingdom's burdens as his own.

sentences.zh: 若必姻親然後可用，則荊州十郡，安得十女婿然後為政哉！

translations.literal: If it must be marriage kin then afterward can be used, then Jing province ten commanderies, how can obtain ten sons-in-law then afterward conduct government!'
translations.idiomatic: If only in-laws may be employed, how could the ten commanderies of Jingzhou ever find ten sons-in-law fit to govern them all?

sentences.zh: 」乃表「陟姻親，舊制不得相監。

translations.literal: Then he memorialized: 'Zhi is marriage kin; by old regulations may not mutually supervise.'
translations.idiomatic: He therefore memorialized again: "Xiahou Zhi is my kinsman by marriage, and precedent forbids such overlap in supervision."

sentences.zh: 皮初之勳宜見酬報。

translations.literal: Pi Chu's merit ought to be seen rewarded.'
translations.idiomatic: Pi Chu's battlefield service deserves a fitting reward.

sentences.zh: 」詔聽之。

translations.literal: An edict heard it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his request.

sentences.zh: 弘於是勸課農桑，寬刑省賦，歲用有年，百姓愛悅。

translations.literal: Hong thereupon urged and inspected farming and sericulture, broadened punishments and reduced levies, years had harvest, the hundred surnames loved and rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong then promoted farming and silk production, eased punishments, and cut taxes until harvests stabilized and the people loved him for it.

sentences.zh: 弘嘗夜起，聞城上持更者歎聲甚苦，遂呼省之。

translations.literal: Hong once rose at night, heard on the wall the watch-holder's sigh sounds very bitter, then called and examined him.
translations.idiomatic: One night Liu Hong rose and heard a night watchman on the wall sighing in deep distress; he had the man summoned and questioned him.

sentences.zh: 兵年過六十，羸疾無襦。

translations.literal: The soldier's years passed sixty, emaciated illness without unlined jacket.
translations.idiomatic: The soldier was over sixty, frail and ill, and had no padded jacket against the cold.

sentences.zh: 弘湣之，乃謫罰主者，遂給韋袍復帽，轉以相付。

translations.literal: Hong pitied him, then punished and fined the responsible chief, then supplied leather robe and lined cap, turned and handed them in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Moved to pity, Liu Hong fined the officer in charge, issued the old man a leather coat and warm cap, and ordered that such gear thereafter be issued in rotation to the watch.

sentences.zh: 舊制，峴方二山澤中不聽百姓捕魚，弘下教曰：「禮，名山大澤不封，與共其利。

translations.literal: Old regulations, in the marshes of the two mountains Xian and Fang did not listen to the hundred surnames catching fish; Hong issued instruction saying: 'By ritual, famous mountains and great marshes are not enclosed, sharing with them the benefit.'
translations.idiomatic: By longstanding rule the lakes between Mount Xian and Mount Fang had been closed to commoners who wished to fish. Liu Hong ordered: "The rites say that famous hills and great marshes must not be monopolized; their bounty belongs to everyone."

sentences.zh: 今公私並兼，百姓無復厝手地，當何謂邪！

translations.literal: Now public and private together seize, the hundred surnames no longer have a place to set hand; what ought this be called!'
translations.idiomatic: Now official and private interests alike have seized those waters, leaving ordinary folk nowhere to earn a living. What sort of policy is that?

sentences.zh: 速改此法。

translations.literal: Speedily change this law.'
translations.idiomatic: Change this regulation at once.

sentences.zh: 」又「酒室中雲齊中酒、聽事酒、猥酒，同用曲米，而優劣三品。

translations.literal: Moreover: 'In the wine chamber are called central-hall wine, audience-hall wine, and coarse wine; they use the same yeast and rice, yet there are three grades of superior and inferior.'
translations.idiomatic: He added: "The government winery labels its stock hall wine, office wine, and common wine, yet all three are brewed from the same grain and starter even though they are sold as three grades of quality."

sentences.zh: 投醪當與三軍同其薄厚，自今不得分別。

translations.literal: Casting ale ought with the three armies share its thin and thick; from now may not discriminate.'
translations.idiomatic: When wine is poured out for the troops it should be the same strength for every rank. Henceforth do not draw petty distinctions.

sentences.zh: 」時益州刺史羅尚為李特所敗，遣使告急，請糧。

translations.literal: At that time Yi province Inspector Luo Shang was by Li Te defeated, sent envoys to report urgency, requesting grain.'
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Luo Shang, the inspector of Yizhou, had been routed by Li Te and sent messengers begging urgently for grain.

sentences.zh: 弘移書贍給，而州府綱紀以運道懸遠，文武匱乏，欲以零陵一運米五千斛與尚。

translations.literal: Hong sent letters to supply, but the province headquarters clerks took the transport route as distant hanging, civil and martial lacking, wished to by Lingling one shipment grain five thousand hu to give to Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong was willing to help, yet his staff officers argued that the supply line was dangerously long and resources thin; they wanted to send Luo Shang only a single consignment of five thousand hu from Lingling.

sentences.zh: 弘曰：「諸君未之思耳。

translations.literal: Hong said: 'Gentlemen have not thought about this.'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong replied, "You are not thinking the matter through."

sentences.zh: 天下一家，彼此無異，吾今給之，則無西顧之憂矣。

translations.literal: All under heaven is one family; this side and that have no difference; I now supply him, then there will be no worry of looking west.'
translations.idiomatic: The empire is one household; west and east are not rivals. If I feed him now, we spare ourselves the worry of what happens on the western frontier later.

sentences.zh: 」遂以零陵米三萬斛給之。

translations.literal: Thereupon by Lingling rice thirty thousand hu gave to him.'
translations.idiomatic: He therefore shipped thirty thousand hu of rice from Lingling to Luo Shang.

sentences.zh: 尚賴以自固。

translations.literal: Shang relied thereby to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang depended on that aid to hold his ground.

sentences.zh: 于時流人在荊州十餘萬戶，羈旅貧乏，多為盜賊。

translations.literal: At that time displaced persons in Jing province were more than ten myriad households, sojourning in poverty and lack, many became bandits and robbers.
translations.idiomatic: At the time well over a hundred thousand refugee households were stranded in Jingzhou, penniless and far from home, and many drifted into banditry.

sentences.zh: 弘乃給其田種糧食，擢其賢才，隨資敘用。

translations.literal: Hong then gave them fields, seed, and grain food, elevated their worthy talents, according to qualifications arranged and employed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong allotted them farmland, seed, and rations, promoted able men among them, and assigned posts according to each man's talents.

sentences.zh: 時總章太樂伶人，避亂多至荊州，或勸可作樂者。

translations.literal: At that time Zongzhang Grand Music performers, fleeing turmoil many arrived in Jing province; some urged that could make music.
translations.idiomatic: Musicians from the imperial Zongzhang and grand music bureaus, fleeing the wars, had flocked to Jingzhou, and some advisers urged Liu Hong to employ them for entertainment.

sentences.zh: 弘曰：「昔劉景升以禮壞樂崩，命杜夔為天子合樂，樂成，欲庭作之。

translations.literal: Hong said: 'Formerly Liu Jingsheng by ritual ruined music collapsed, ordered Du Kui for the Son of Heaven to compose music; when music was completed, wished to perform it in the courtyard.'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong answered: "Long ago Liu Biao, claiming that rites had collapsed and music with them, ordered Du Kui to compose a new court suite for the emperor. When it was finished Liu Biao wanted it played in his own courtyard."

sentences.zh: 夔曰：'為天子合樂而庭作之，恐非將軍本意。

translations.literal: Kui said: 'For the Son of Heaven composing music yet performing it in the courtyard, I fear is not the general's original intent.'
translations.idiomatic: Du Kui replied, 'Music written for the Son of Heaven should not debut in a provincial courtyard; I doubt that was what you intended.'

sentences.zh: '吾常為之歎息。

translations.literal: I always for it sighed and sighed.'
translations.idiomatic: I have never ceased to sigh over that story.

sentences.zh: 今主上蒙塵，吾未能展效臣節，雖有家伎，猶不宜聽，況禦樂哉！

translations.literal: Now the ruler above is covered in dust; I have been unable to display and enact ministerial integrity; although there are household entertainers, still it is not fitting to listen, how much more imperial music!'
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign is still in exile and I have yet to prove my loyalty as a minister. Even private entertainments would be out of place, let alone the music of the imperial orchestra!

sentences.zh: 」乃下郡縣，使安慰之，須朝廷旋返，送還本署。

translations.literal: Then issued to commanderies and counties, causing to comfort them, wait until the court returns turning, send back to original bureaus.'
translations.idiomatic: He therefore instructed the local authorities to comfort the musicians and hold them until the court returned to Luoyang, when they could be sent back to their original posts.

sentences.zh: 論平張昌功，應封次子一人縣侯，弘上疏固讓，許之。

translations.literal: Judging the merit of pacifying Zhang Chang, ought to enfeoff one second son as county marquis; Hong submitted memorial firmly declining; it was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: For his part in crushing Zhang Chang he was entitled to have a second son enfeoffed as a county marquis, but Liu Hong repeatedly declined the honor until the throne accepted his refusal.

sentences.zh: 進拜侍中、鎮南大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Was advanced and appointed palace attendant, grand general who guards the south, with establishment of office equal to the three excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace attendant, grand general who guards the south, with the privilege of an independent headquarters equated to the three senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 惠帝幸長安，河間王顒挾天子，詔弘為劉喬繼援。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui visited Chang'an; the Prince of Hejian Yong held the Son of Heaven; an edict ordered Hong as Liu Qiao's successor aid.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hui was taken to Chang'an and Prince Sima Yong of Hejian held the emperor hostage, an edict instructed Liu Hong to march in support of Liu Qiao.

sentences.zh: 弘以張方殘暴，知顒必敗，遣使受東海王越節度。

translations.literal: Hong by Zhang Fang's cruelty and violence, knew Yong must be defeated, sent envoys to receive the Prince of Donghai Yue's regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Judging Zhang Fang's brutality a sign that Sima Yong could not last, Liu Hong sent messengers to place himself under Prince Sima Yue of the Eastern Sea.

sentences.zh: 時天下大亂，弘專督江漢，威行南服。

translations.literal: At that time all under heaven was greatly chaotic; Hong alone supervised the Yang and Han, awe extended through the southern garments.
translations.idiomatic: While the realm dissolved into chaos, Liu Hong alone commanded the middle Yangzi and Han river basins, and his authority ran unchecked through the south.

sentences.zh: 前廣漢太守辛冉說弘以從橫之事，弘大怒，斬之。

translations.literal: Former Guanghan prefect Xin Ran persuaded Hong with vertical-horizontal affairs; Hong was greatly angry and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Ran, the former prefect of Guanghan, tried to draw him into a scheme of shifting alliances; Liu Hong flew into a rage and executed him.

sentences.zh: 河間王顒使張光為順陽太守，南陽太守衛展說弘曰：「彭城王前東奔，有不善之言。

translations.literal: The Prince of Hejian Yong sent Zhang Guang as Shunyang prefect; Nanyang prefect Wei Zhan said to Hong: 'The Prince of Pengcheng formerly fled east, had not good words.'
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sima Yong of Hejian had appointed Zhang Guang prefect of Shunyang. Wei Zhan, the prefect of Nanyang, urged Liu Hong: "When the prince of Pengcheng fled eastward he spoke slanderously of your intentions."

sentences.zh: 張光，太宰腹心，宜斬光以明向背。

translations.literal: Zhang Guang is the grand tutor's belly heart; ought behead Guang to clarify turning back or not.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guang is a trusted confidant of the grand tutor; execute him to show where you stand.

sentences.zh: 」弘曰：「宰輔得失，豈張光之罪！

translations.literal: Hong said: 'The chief minister's gain and loss, how can it be Zhang Guang's crime!'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong retorted, "Whether the chief counselor is right or wrong is hardly Zhang Guang's fault."

sentences.zh: 危人自安，君子弗為也。

translations.literal: Endangering others to secure oneself, the gentleman does not do.'
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman does not buy his own safety by murdering another man.

sentences.zh: 」展深恨之。

translations.literal: Zhan deeply hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhan nursed a bitter grudge against him from that day on.

sentences.zh: 陳敏寇揚州，引兵欲西上，弘乃解南蠻，以授前北軍中候蔣超，統江夏太守陶侃、武陵太守苗光，以大眾屯于夏口。

translations.literal: Chen Min raided Yang province, led troops wishing to go west upward; Hong then dissolved Southern Man, to give to former Northern Army middle guard Jiang Chao, commanding Jiangxia prefect Tao Kan, Wuling prefect Miao Guang, with great masses garrisoned at Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Min invaded Yangzhou and marched west, Liu Hong transferred the southern tribes commission to Jiang Chao, former captain of the central camp of the northern army, and massed a large force—including Tao Kan, prefect of Jiangxia, and Miao Guang, prefect of Wuling—at Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 又遣治中何松領建平、宜都、襄陽三郡兵，屯巴東，為羅尚後繼。

translations.literal: Also sent administrative supervisor He Song leading Jianping, Yidu, and Xiangyang three commanderies' troops, garrisoned at Badong, as Luo Shang's rear successor.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent his administrative aide He Song with troops from the three commanderies of Jianping, Yidu, and Xiangyang to encamp at Badong as a second line behind Luo Shang.

sentences.zh: 又加南平太守應詹甯遠將軍，督三郡水軍，繼蔣超。

translations.literal: Also added Nanping prefect Ying Zhan as General Who Pacifies the Distance, supervised three commanderies' water army, succeeding Jiang Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Zhan, prefect of Nanping, was further named general who pacifies the distance and placed in command of the riverine forces of three commanderies to follow Jiang Chao.

sentences.zh: 侃與敏同郡，又同歲舉吏，或有間侃者，弘不疑之。

translations.literal: Kan and Min were same commandery, also same year raised as clerks; some had slander against Kan; Hong did not suspect him.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan came from the same commandery as Chen Min and had entered official service in the same year, which led some to whisper that he might defect, yet Liu Hong never doubted him.

sentences.zh: 乃以侃為前鋒督護，委以討敏之任。

translations.literal: Then by Kan as vanguard protector, entrusted him with the duty of attacking Min.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore named Tao Kan vanguard commander and gave him full responsibility for the campaign against Chen Min.

sentences.zh: 侃遣子及兄子為質，弘遣之曰：「賢叔征行，君祖母年高，便可歸也。

translations.literal: Kan sent son and elder brother's son as hostages; Hong sent them away saying: 'Your worthy uncle on campaign, your grandmother's years are high; you may return.'
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan sent his son and nephew as hostages, but Liu Hong sent the boys home, saying, "Your uncle is on campaign and your grandmother is elderly; take this chance to go back to her."

sentences.zh: 匹夫之交尚不負心，何況大丈夫乎！

translations.literal: A common fellow's friendship still does not betray the heart, how much more a great man!'
translations.idiomatic: Even commoners keep faith among friends; would a man of true stature do less?

sentences.zh: 」陳敏竟不敢窺境。

translations.literal: Chen Min in the end did not dare to spy on the border.'
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min never dared test Liu Hong's frontier again.

sentences.zh: 永興三年，詔進號車騎將軍，開府及餘官如故。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxing, an edict advanced his title to chariot and cavalry general; establishment of office and remaining offices as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Yongxing era an edict raised his rank to general of chariots and cavalry while leaving his other titles, including the independent headquarters, unchanged.

sentences.zh: 弘每有興廢，手書守相，丁寧款密，所以人皆感悅，爭赴之，咸曰：「得劉公一紙書，賢於十部從事。

translations.literal: Whenever Hong had raising and abolishing, he personally wrote to prefects and chancellors, earnestly intimate; therefore people all were moved and pleased, competed to go to him, all said: 'Obtaining Lord Liu one sheet of writing is worthier than ten departments of attendants.'
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Liu Hong instituted or abolished a policy he wrote personally to each local governor, his tone warm and meticulous. Officials vied to carry out his wishes and used to say, "One letter from Lord Liu is worth more than ten staff supervisors combined."

sentences.zh: 」及東海王越奉迎大駕，弘遣參軍劉盤為督護，率諸軍會之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Donghai Yue welcomed the great chariot, Hong sent adjutant Liu Pan as protector, leading the various armies to join him.'
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Sima Yue of the Eastern Sea went to escort the imperial carriage eastward, Liu Hong sent his adjutant Liu Pan as coordinator of the allied forces to join him.

sentences.zh: 盤既旋，弘自以老疾，將解州及校尉，適分授所部，未及表上，卒於襄陽。

translations.literal: When Pan had returned, Hong himself by old age and illness, was about to resign province and colonel, was about to divide and confer on subordinates, had not yet reached memorializing upward, died at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Pan came home, Liu Hong—feeling the weight of age and illness—planned to surrender the provincial seal and the colonelcy and divide authority among his subordinates, but he died at Xiangyang before the memorial could be sent.

sentences.zh: 士女嗟痛，若喪所親矣。

translations.literal: Gentry and women sighed in pain, as if having lost those they were close to.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women throughout the region mourned as though they had lost a parent.

sentences.zh: 初，成都王穎南奔，欲之本國，弘距之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Prince of Chengdu Ying fled south, wished to his original state; Hong resisted him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Prince Sima Ying of Chengdu fled south hoping to reach his princedom, Liu Hong barred his path.

sentences.zh: 及弘卒，弘司馬郭勱欲推穎為主，弘子璠追遵弘志，於是墨絰率府兵計勱，戰于濁水，斬之，襄沔肅清，初，東海王越疑弘與劉喬貳於己，雖下節度，心未能安。

translations.literal: When Hong died, Hong's Major Guo Li wished to establish Ying as lord; Hong's son Fan pursued and followed Hong's intent; thereupon in ink mourning sash led prefectural troops to attack Li, battled at Zhuoshui, beheaded him, Xiang and Mian were cleared; earlier, the Prince of Donghai Yue suspected Hong and Liu Qiao of being double toward himself, although issued regulation, in heart could not be at ease.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Hong died his marshal Guo Li tried to proclaim Sima Ying as ruler, but Liu Hong's son Liu Fan, determined to honor his father's loyalty, donned mourning black, led the headquarters troops against Guo Li, defeated him on the Zhuo River, and took his head, restoring calm to the Xiang and Mian region. Even so, Prince Sima Yue of the Eastern Sea had long suspected Liu Hong and Liu Qiao of divided loyalty: though he issued orders placing them under his command, he never quite trusted them.

sentences.zh: 及弘距穎，璠又斬勵，朝廷嘉之。

translations.literal: When Hong resisted Ying, Fan again beheaded Li, and the court praised it.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Hong blocked Sima Ying's advance, Liu Fan struck down Guo Li as well; the court commended their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 越手書與璠讚美之，表贈弘新城郡公，諡曰元。

translations.literal: Yue personally wrote to Fan praising him, memorialized posthumously enfeoffing Hong as duke of Xincheng commandery, posthumous title Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue wrote Liu Fan a personal letter of praise, and a memorial followed posthumously enfeoffing Liu Hong as duke of Xincheng with the posthumous epithet "Primordial" (Yuan).

sentences.zh: 陶侃，字士行，本鄱陽人也。

translations.literal: Tao Kan, courtesy name Shixing, was originally a man of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan, whose courtesy name was Shixing, was a native of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 吳平，徙家廬江之尋陽。

translations.literal: When Wu was pacified, moved family to Xunyang in Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest of Wu his family relocated to Xunyang in Lujiang commandery.

sentences.zh: 父丹，吳揚武將軍。

translations.literal: His father Dan was General Who Displays Martial Might under Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Tao Dan, had served the kingdom of Wu as general who displays martial might.

sentences.zh: 侃早孤貧，為縣吏。

translations.literal: Kan was early orphaned and poor, and became a county clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan lost his father while still young and grew up in poverty, taking work as a county clerk.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽孝廉範逵嘗過侃，時倉卒無以待賓，其母乃截髪得雙髲，以易酒肴，樂飲極歡，雖僕從亦過所望。

translations.literal: Poyang filially incorrupt Fan Kui once passed Kan; at the time hastily there was nothing to await a guest; his mother then cut hair to obtain paired coils, thereby to exchange for wine and dishes, joyfully drank to utmost delight; although servants also exceeded what was hoped.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Kui, a filially exemplary candidate from Poyang, visited Tao Kan unexpectedly, the household had nothing fit to serve a guest. Tao Kan's mother cut off her hair and sold the coils it yielded to buy wine and food. The party grew merry, and even the servants received more kindness than they had expected.

sentences.zh: 及逵去，侃追送百餘里。

translations.literal: When Kui departed, Kan pursued and escorted more than a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Kui left, Tao Kan accompanied him on foot for over a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 逵曰：「卿欲仕郡乎？

translations.literal: Kui said: 'Do you wish to serve in the commandery?'
translations.idiomatic: Fan Kui asked him, "Do you hope to take office in the commandery?"

sentences.zh: 」侃曰：「欲之，困於無津耳。

translations.literal: Kan said: 'I wish it, but am trapped by having no ford.'
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan answered, "I do—but I am stranded with no bridge across."

sentences.zh: 」逵過廬江太守張夔，稱美之。

translations.literal: Kui passed the Lujiang prefect Zhang Kui and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Kui then called on Prefect Zhang Kui of Lujiang and spoke warmly of Tao Kan.

sentences.zh: 夔召為督郵，領樅陽令。

translations.literal: Kui summoned him as postal inspector, concurrently magistrate of Zongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kui appointed him postal inspector and acting magistrate of Zongyang.

sentences.zh: 有能名，遷主簿。

translations.literal: He had a reputation for ability, was promoted to chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He earned a name for competence and was promoted to chief clerk of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 會州部從事之郡，欲有所按，侃閉門部勒諸吏，謂從事曰：「若鄙郡有違，自當明憲直繩，不宜相逼。

translations.literal: When the provincial investigator came to the commandery wishing to conduct some inquiry, Kan closed the gate and marshaled the clerks, saying to the investigator: 'If our humble commandery has violations, we should ourselves clarify the statutes and straighten the cord; it is not fitting to press each other.'
translations.idiomatic: When a provincial investigator arrived intent on finding fault, Tao Kan barred the gates, assembled the clerks, and told the man, "If our commandery has erred, we will answer to the law ourselves; you need not hound us."

sentences.zh: 若不以禮，吾能禦之。

translations.literal: If you refuse courtesy, I can resist you.
translations.idiomatic: If you refuse common courtesy, I can resist you myself.

sentences.zh: 」從事即退。

translations.literal: The investigator then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The investigator withdrew at once.

sentences.zh: 夔妻有疾，將迎醫於數百里。

translations.literal: Kui's wife had illness; he was about to welcome a physician from several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kui's wife fell ill, and he planned to fetch a physician from hundreds of li away.

sentences.zh: 時正寒雪，諸綱紀皆難之，侃獨曰：「資于事父以事君。

translations.literal: At the time it was exactly cold snow; all the clerks found it difficult; Kan alone said: 'By what serves in serving a father to serve a lord.'
translations.idiomatic: A blizzard was blowing, and every clerk shrank from the errand. Tao Kan alone said, "The same devotion one owes a father one owes a ruler."

sentences.zh: 小君，猶母也，安有父母之疾而不盡心乎！

translations.literal: The lesser lord is still like a mother; how can there be parents' illness and not exhaust the heart!
translations.idiomatic: The mistress of the house is like a mother to us: how could we ignore her illness and withhold our utmost care?

sentences.zh: 」乃請行。

translations.literal: Then requested to go.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore volunteered to make the journey.

sentences.zh: 眾咸服其義。

translations.literal: The crowd all submitted to his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The others, ashamed, conceded the moral point.

sentences.zh: 長沙太守萬嗣過廬江，見侃，虛心敬悅，曰：「君終當有大名。

translations.literal: Changsha prefect Wan Si passed Lujiang, saw Kan, was empty-hearted respectful and pleased, said: 'You in the end will have a great name.'
translations.idiomatic: When Wan Si, prefect of Changsha, passed through Lujiang and met Tao Kan, he was struck with sincere respect and said, "You are destined for a great reputation."

sentences.zh: 」命其子與之結友而去。

translations.literal: Ordered his son to befriend him and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He told his son to befriend Tao Kan and then continued his journey.

sentences.zh: 夔察侃為孝廉，至洛陽，數詣張華。

translations.literal: Kui nominated Kan as filially incorrupt; arriving at Luoyang, repeatedly visited Zhang Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kui recommended Tao Kan as filially exemplary, and in Luoyang Tao Kan called several times on Zhang Hua.

sentences.zh: 華初以遠人，不甚接遇。

translations.literal: Hua at first by him being a man from afar, did not much receive and treat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua at first treated him coolly, thinking him a provincial outsider.

sentences.zh: 侃每往，神無忤色。

translations.literal: Whenever Kan went, his spirit had no offending color.
translations.idiomatic: Yet each visit found Tao Kan calm and unresentful.

sentences.zh: 華後與語，異之。

translations.literal: Hua afterward conversed with him and marveled.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Hua finally spoke with him at length, he was astonished by his quality.

sentences.zh: 除郎中。

translations.literal: Was appointed gentleman of the interior.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan was appointed gentleman of the interior.

sentences.zh: 伏波將軍孫秀以亡國支庶，府望不顯，中華人士恥為掾屬，以侃寒宦，召為舍人。

translations.literal: General Who Calms the Waves Sun Xiu, by being a fallen state's collateral branch, his headquarters prestige was not prominent; central plain gentlemen were ashamed to be clerks; by Kan's humble office, summoned him as retainer.
translations.idiomatic: General Sun Xiu, a collateral descendant of a conquered dynasty, commanded little prestige, and men of the central plains disdained posts in his staff; because Tao Kan came from a humble background, Sun Xiu recruited him as a household retainer.

sentences.zh: 時豫章國郎中令楊晫，侃州裏也，為鄉論所歸。

translations.literal: At the time Yuzhang kingdom gentleman-director Yang Zhuo, Kan's same commandery man, was what village opinion returned to.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhuo, the gentleman-director of the princedom of Yuzhang, hailed from the same region as Tao Kan and enjoyed wide local esteem.

sentences.zh: 侃詣之，晫曰：「《易》稱'貞固足以幹事'，陶士行是也。

translations.literal: Kan visited him; Zhuo said: 'The Changes states "Firm correctness suffices to accomplish affairs"—Tao Shixing is such a one.'
translations.idiomatic: When Tao Kan called on him, Yang Zhuo said, "The Book of Changes praises steadfast integrity that can carry great tasks—Tao Shixing is exactly that sort of man."

sentences.zh: 」與同乘見中書郎顧榮，榮甚奇之。

translations.literal: Together they rode in a carriage to see Secretariat gentleman Gu Rong; Rong greatly marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: He took Tao Kan in his carriage to meet Gu Rong of the secretariat, who was greatly impressed.

sentences.zh: 吏部郎溫雅謂晫曰：「奈何與小人共載？

translations.literal: Personnel ministry gentleman Wen Ya said to Zhuo: 'Why ride together with a petty man?'
translations.idiomatic: Wen Ya of the ministry of personnel asked Yang Zhuo, "Why share a carriage with a nobody?"

sentences.zh: 」晫曰：「此人非凡器也。

translations.literal: Zhuo said: 'This person is not a common vessel.'
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhuo replied, "This man is no ordinary vessel."

sentences.zh: 」尚書樂廣欲會荊揚士人，武庫令黃慶進侃於廣。

translations.literal: Minister Yue Guang wished to convene gentlemen of Jing and Yang; arsenal director Huang Qing advanced Kan to Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Yue Guang planned a gathering of scholars from Jingzhou and Yangzhou, and Huang Qing, director of the arsenal, recommended Tao Kan to him.

sentences.zh: 人或非之，慶曰：「此子終當遠到，復何疑也！

translations.literal: Some criticized this; Qing said: 'This lad in the end will go far; what doubt remains!'
translations.idiomatic: Some objected, but Huang Qing said, "That young man will rise very high indeed—mark my words!"

translations.literal: (Closing quotation mark.)
translations.idiomatic: Such was the end of Huang Qing's remark.

sentences.zh: 慶後為吏部令史，舉侃補武岡令。

translations.literal: Qing afterward became a ministry clerk and nominated Kan to supplement as magistrate of Wugang.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Qing later served as a clerk in the ministry of personnel and recommended Tao Kan for appointment as magistrate of Wugang.

sentences.zh: 與太守呂岳有嫌，棄官歸，為郡小中正。

translations.literal: He had a grudge with prefect Lu Yue, abandoned office and returned, became minor impartial judge of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He quarreled with Prefect Lu Yue, resigned his post, and at home was named a minor impartial judge for the commandery.

sentences.zh: 會劉弘為荊州刺史，將之官，辟侃為南蠻長史，遣先向襄陽討賊張昌，破之。

translations.literal: When Liu Hong became Inspector of Jing province, about to go to office, summoned Kan as chief clerk for the southern tribes, sent him first toward Xiangyang to attack bandit Zhang Chang, and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Hong took up the inspectorship of Jingzhou, he summoned Tao Kan as chief clerk for the southern tribes and sent him ahead to Xiangyang to strike the rebel Zhang Chang, whom he crushed.

sentences.zh: 弘既至，謂侃曰：「吾昔為羊公參軍，謂吾其後當居身處。

translations.literal: When Hong had arrived, he said to Kan: 'In the past when I was adjutant to Duke Yang, he said that afterward I would occupy his place.'
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Hong reached his post he told Tao Kan, "Long ago, as adjutant to Yang Hu, I was told I would one day stand in his shoes."

sentences.zh: 今相觀察，必繼老夫矣。

translations.literal: Now observing you, you must succeed this old man.
translations.idiomatic: Watching you now, I see that you will succeed this old man of mine.

sentences.zh: 」後以軍功封東鄉侯，邑千戶。

translations.literal: Afterward by military merit was enfeoffed marquis of Dongxiang, fief of a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for military merit, he was enfeoffed as marquis of Dongxiang with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 陳敏之亂，弘以侃為江夏太守，加鷹揚將軍。

translations.literal: During Chen Min's rebellion, Hong by Kan as prefect of Jiangxia, added General Who Displays the Hawk's Might.
translations.idiomatic: During Chen Min's revolt Liu Hong appointed Tao Kan prefect of Jiangxia with the additional title general who displays the hawk's might.

sentences.zh: 侃備威儀，迎母官舍，鄉里榮之。

translations.literal: Kan prepared full regalia and welcomed his mother to the official residence; the village honored it.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan received his mother into the official residence with full ceremony, to the admiration of his home district.

sentences.zh: 敏遣其弟恢來寇武昌，侃出兵禦之。

translations.literal: Min sent his younger brother Hui to raid Wuchang; Kan led troops to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min dispatched his brother Chen Hui against Wuchang, and Tao Kan marched to meet him.

sentences.zh: 隨郡內史扈瑰間侃於弘曰：「侃與敏有鄉里之舊，居大郡，統強兵，脫有異志，則荊州無東門矣。

translations.literal: Suizhou inner governor Hu Gui slandered Kan to Hong, saying: 'Kan has old village ties with Min, holds a great commandery, commands strong troops; if perchance he has a different intent, then Jingzhou will have no eastern gate.'
translations.idiomatic: Hu Gui, inner governor of Suizhou, whispered to Liu Hong that Tao Kan's old ties to Chen Min, combined with a large command and crack troops, might turn disloyal and shut Jingzhou's eastern gate.

sentences.zh: 」弘曰：「侃之忠能，吾得之已久，豈有是乎！

translations.literal: Hong said: 'Kan's loyalty and ability—I have long known them; how could there be this!'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong replied, "I have known Tao Kan's loyalty and competence for years. Do not speak such nonsense."

sentences.zh: 」侃潛聞之，遽遣子洪及兄子臻詣弘以自固。

translations.literal: Kan secretly heard it, hastily sent son Hong and elder brother's son Zhen to Hong to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao Kan overheard the rumor, he immediately sent his son Tao Hong and his nephew Tao Zhen to Liu Hong to reaffirm his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 弘引為參軍，資而遣之。

translations.literal: Hong appointed them adjutants, supplied them, and sent them off.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong enrolled them as adjutants, gave them provisions, and sent them back.

sentences.zh: 又加侃為督護，使與諸軍並力距恢。

translations.literal: Also added Kan as protector, causing him with the various armies jointly to resist Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong further named Tao Kan protector of the army and ordered him to join the other commands against Chen Hui.

sentences.zh: 侃乃以運船為戰艦，或言不可，侃曰：「用官物討官賊，但須列上有本末耳。

translations.literal: Kan then used transport boats as war vessels; some said it could not be done; Kan said: 'Using official goods to attack official bandits, one only needs to report the whole story upward.'
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan converted grain barges into warships. When others objected, he said, "We are spending public equipment to crush public enemies—so long as we report the facts to the throne, it is lawful."

sentences.zh: 」於是擊恢，所向必破。

translations.literal: Thereupon attacked Hui; wherever aimed, necessarily broke.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Chen Hui and shattered every formation he met.

sentences.zh: 侃戎政齊肅，凡有虜獲，皆分士卒，身無私焉。

translations.literal: Kan's military administration was orderly and stern; whenever there were captives, all he divided among the soldiers; personally he had none.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan ran a disciplined camp: all booty went to the troops, and he took none for himself.

sentences.zh: 後以母憂去職。

translations.literal: Afterward by mother's mourning left office.
translations.idiomatic: He later resigned to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 嘗有二客來吊，不哭而退，化為雙鶴，沖天而去，時人異之。

translations.literal: Once two guests came to condole, did not weep but withdrew, transformed into paired cranes, rushed skyward and departed; people of the time marveled.
translations.idiomatic: Once two mourners called, left without weeping, and were seen to mount into the sky as a pair of cranes—an omen people found uncanny.

sentences.zh: 服闋，參東海王越軍事。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, joined Prince of the Eastern Sea Yue's military staff.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended he joined the military staff of Prince Sima Yue of the Eastern Sea.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史華軼表侃為揚武將軍，使屯夏口，又以臻為參軍。

translations.literal: Jiangzhou Inspector Hua Yi memorialized Kan as General Who Displays Martial Might, caused him to garrison Xiakou, and also made Zhen an adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Yi, inspector of Jiangzhou, recommended Tao Kan as general who displays martial might and stationed him at Xiakou while appointing Tao Zhen his adjutant.

sentences.zh: 軼與元帝素不平，臻懼難作，托疾而歸，白侃曰：「華彥夏有憂天下之志，而才不足，且與琅邪不平，難將作矣。

translations.literal: Yi and the Prince of Langya were long not at peace; Zhen feared trouble would arise, feigned illness and returned, reporting to Kan: 'Hua Yancxia has the will to worry for the realm, but his talent is insufficient, and he is not at peace with the Prince of Langya; disaster will arise.'
translations.idiomatic: Because Hua Yi and the Prince of Langya were on bad terms, Tao Zhen pretended illness, hurried home, and warned Tao Kan that Hua Yi, though public-spirited, lacked the ability to stand against the prince of Langya—trouble was brewing.

sentences.zh: 」侃怒，遣臻還軼。

translations.literal: Kan was angry and sent Zhen back to Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan angrily sent Tao Zhen back to Hua Yi.

sentences.zh: 臻遂東歸於帝。

translations.literal: Zhen then went east to join the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Zhen instead went east to offer his service to the future Yuan emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝見之，大悅，命臻為參軍，加侃奮威將軍，假赤幢曲蓋軺車、鼓吹。

translations.literal: When the emperor saw him, was greatly pleased, ordered Zhen as adjutant, added Kan General Who Rouses Might, with credential crimson banner, curved canopy light cart, and band.
translations.idiomatic: The prince received him gladly, made Tao Zhen an adjutant, and bestowed on Tao Kan the titles general who rouses might together with the insignia of crimson banner, curved canopy carriage, and a military band.

sentences.zh: 侃乃與華軼告絕。

translations.literal: Kan then broke relations with Hua Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan thereupon severed ties with Hua Yi.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷龍驤將軍、武昌太守。

translations.literal: Before long, was promoted General Who Soars like the Dragon and prefect of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to general who soars like the dragon and prefect of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 時天下饑荒，山夷多斷江劫掠。

translations.literal: At the time all under heaven had famine; mountain barbarians often cut the river and plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Famine gripped the empire, and hill tribesmen constantly blocked the river to rob convoys.

sentences.zh: 侃令諸將詐作商船以誘之。

translations.literal: Kan ordered the generals to feign merchant ships to lure them.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan ordered his officers to disguise warships as merchant craft to bait them.

sentences.zh: 劫果至，生獲數人，是西陽王羕之左右。

translations.literal: When the bandits indeed arrived, alive captured several persons; they were the attendants of the Prince of Xiyang, Rong.
translations.idiomatic: When the raiders struck, his men took prisoners who proved to be retainers of Prince Sima Rong of Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 侃即遣兵逼羕，令出向賊，侃整陣於釣台為後繼。

translations.literal: Kan immediately sent troops to press Rong, ordering him to march against the bandits; Kan arrayed his formation at Diaotai as rear support.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan immediately pressured Prince Rong to drive the brigands out while Tao Kan himself formed a battle line at Diaotai as rear guard.

sentences.zh: 羕縛送帳下二十人，侃斬之。

translations.literal: Rong bound and sent twenty men under his tent; Kan beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rong handed over twenty household guards; Tao Kan executed them all.

sentences.zh: 自是水陸肅清，流亡者歸之盈路，侃竭資振給焉。

translations.literal: From this water and land were cleared; displaced persons returned to him filling the roads; Kan exhausted his resources to relieve and supply them.
translations.idiomatic: River and road traffic became safe again, and refugees flocked back until the highways were crowded; Tao Kan spent his own funds to feed them.

sentences.zh: 又立夷市於郡東，大收其利。

translations.literal: Also established a barbarian market east of the commandery, greatly collecting its profits.
translations.idiomatic: He also opened a frontier market east of the city and drew large revenue from it.

sentences.zh: 而帝使侃擊杜弢，令振威將軍周訪、廣武將軍趙誘受侃節度。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the emperor ordered Kan to attack Du Tao, ordering General Who Rouses Terror Zhou Fang and General Who Displays Martial Valor Zhao You to receive Kan's command.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered him against Du Tao, with Generals Zhou Fang and Zhao You placed under his orders.

sentences.zh: 侃令二將為前鋒，兄子輿為左甄，擊賊，破之。

translations.literal: Kan ordered the two generals as vanguard, elder brother's son Yu as left horn, attacked the bandits, defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He made the two generals his van, his nephew Tao Yu the left horn, and smashed the enemy host.

sentences.zh: 時周顗為荊州刺史，先鎮潯水城，賊掠其良口。

translations.literal: At the time Zhou Yi was Inspector of Jing province, first garrisoned Xunshui city; the bandits plundered his good people.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yi, inspector of Jingzhou, had been holding Xunshui fort when the rebels carried off his people.

sentences.zh: 侃使部將硃伺救之，賊退保泠口。

translations.literal: Kan sent subordinate general Zhu Si to rescue them; the bandits withdrew to defend Lengkou.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan sent Zhu Si to relieve him, and the raiders fell back to Lengkou.

sentences.zh: 侃謂諸將曰：「此賊必更步向武昌，吾宜還城，晝夜三日行可至。

translations.literal: Kan said to the generals: 'This bandit will surely again march toward Wuchang on foot; I ought to return to the city; in three days' day-and-night march we can arrive.'
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan told his officers, "The enemy will march overland toward Wuchang. We must regain the city—a forced march can bring us there in three days."

sentences.zh: 卿等認能忍饑鬥邪？

translations.literal: Can you gentlemen endure hunger and still fight?
translations.idiomatic: Can you endure hunger long enough to fight them off?

sentences.zh: 」部將吳寄曰：「要欲十日忍饑，晝當擊賊，夜分捕魚，足以相濟。

translations.literal: Subordinate general Wu Ji said: 'We require ten days of enduring hunger; by day we strike the bandits, by night we split up to fish—that suffices to help each other.'
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ji answered, "Give us ten days of hunger: we will fight by daylight and fish by night—that will keep us fed."

sentences.zh: 」侃曰：「卿健將也。

translations.literal: Kan said: 'You are a stalwart commander.'
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan said, "You are the kind of officer I need."

sentences.zh: 」賊果增兵來攻，侃使硃伺等逆擊，大破之，獲其輜重，殺傷甚眾。

translations.literal: The bandits indeed increased troops to attack; Kan ordered Zhu Si and others to strike them head-on, greatly defeated them, captured their baggage, killed and wounded very many.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy did reinforce and attack, but Zhu Si's counterstroke routed them, seized their baggage train, and inflicted heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 遣參軍王貢告捷于王敦，敦曰：「若無陶侯，便失荊州矣。

translations.literal: Sent adjutant Wang Gong to report victory to Wang Dun; Dun said: 'If not for Lord Tao, Jingzhou would have been lost.'
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wang Gong to report to Wang Dun, who said, "Without Lord Tao we would already have lost Jingzhou."

sentences.zh: 伯仁方入境，便為賊所破，不知那得刺史？

translations.literal: Boren had barely entered the territory when he was broken by bandits—how could there be an inspector?
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yi had scarcely crossed the border when the rebels smashed him—where was our inspector then?

sentences.zh: 」貢對曰：「鄙州方有事難，非陶龍驤莫可。

translations.literal: Gong replied: 'Our humble province is in crisis; without General Tao the Dragon Soarer it cannot be saved.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong answered, "Our province is in extremis; only General Tao the Dragon Soarer can save it."

sentences.zh: 」敦然之，即表拜侃為使持節、甯遠將軍、南蠻校尉、荊州刺史，領西陽、江夏、武昌，鎮於沌口，又移入沔江。

translations.literal: Dun approved, immediately memorialized appointing Kan as bearer of the staff of authority, General Who Pacifies the Distance, Colonel of the Southern Man, Inspector of Jing province, concurrently in charge of Xiyang, Jiangxia, and Wuchang, garrisoned at Dunkou, then moved into the Mian River.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun agreed and at once recommended Tao Kan as commissioner with full authority, general who pacifies the distance, colonel of the southern tribes, and inspector of Jingzhou, overseeing Xiyang, Jiangxia, and Wuchang from a base first at Dunkou and later on the Mian River.

sentences.zh: 遣硃伺等討江夏賊，殺之。

translations.literal: Sent Zhu Si and others to attack Jiangxia bandits and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Zhu Si against the Jiangxia bandits and destroyed them.

sentences.zh: 賊王沖自稱荊州刺史，據江陵。

translations.literal: Bandit Wang Chong styled himself Inspector of Jing province and occupied Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: A rebel named Wang Chong proclaimed himself inspector of Jingzhou and seized Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 王貢還，至竟陵，矯侃命，以杜曾為前鋒大督護，進軍斬沖，悉降其眾。

translations.literal: When Wang Gong returned, reaching Jingling, he forged Kan's orders, making Du Zeng grand vanguard protector, advanced the army, beheaded Chong, and all his masses surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On his way back Wang Gong stopped at Jingling, forged orders in Tao Kan's name, appointed Du Zeng grand vanguard protector, advanced, executed Wang Chong, and absorbed his army.

sentences.zh: 侃召曾不到，貢又恐矯命獲罪，遂與曾舉兵反，擊侃督護鄭攀于沌陽，破之，又敗硃伺於沔口。

translations.literal: Kan summoned Zeng but he did not arrive; Gong again feared forging orders would incur guilt, then with Zeng raised troops in rebellion, attacked Kan's protector Zheng Pan at Zhenyang, defeated him, and again defeated Zhu Si at Hankou.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao Kan summoned Du Zeng and he failed to appear, Wang Gong feared punishment for his forgery and joined Du Zeng in revolt. They struck Tao Kan's protector Zheng Pan at Zhenyang, routed him, and then defeated Zhu Si at the Han estuary.

sentences.zh: 侃欲退入溳中，部將張奕將貳於侃，詭說曰：「賊至而動，眾必不可。

translations.literal: Kan wished to withdraw into the Yun basin; subordinate general Zhang Yi was about to betray Kan, deceitfully said: 'When the bandits arrive then moving, the host certainly cannot.'
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan prepared to pull back into the Yun valley, but Zhang Yi, plotting defection, falsely urged him, "If you wait until the enemy is upon you before moving, the army will never hold."

sentences.zh: 」侃惑之而不進。

translations.literal: Kan was confused by this and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan accepted the advice and halted his advance.

sentences.zh: 無何，賊至，果為所敗。

translations.literal: Before long, the bandits arrived and he was indeed defeated by them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels soon arrived and routed him.

sentences.zh: 賊鉤侃所乘艦，侃窘急，走入小船。

translations.literal: The bandits hooked the ship Kan rode; Kan was pressed and hurried, ran into a small boat.
translations.idiomatic: They grappled Tao Kan's flagship; in desperation he scrambled into a skiff.

sentences.zh: 硃伺力戰，僅而獲免。

translations.literal: Zhu Si fought with strength, barely thereby escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Si fought a desperate rear-guard action so that Tao Kan barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 張奕竟奔於賊。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi in the end fled to the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi ultimately deserted to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 侃坐免官。

translations.literal: Kan by sitting offense was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan was stripped of his titles for the defeat.

sentences.zh: 王敦表以侃白衣領職。

translations.literal: Wang Dun memorialized that Kan in plain clothes should hold the post.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun asked the throne to let Tao Kan retain the command in civilian dress.

sentences.zh: 侃復率周訪等進軍人湘，使都尉楊舉為先驅，擊杜弢，大破之，屯兵於城西。

translations.literal: Kan again led Zhou Fang and others to advance the army into Xiang; sent commandant Yang Ju as vanguard, attacked Du Tao, greatly defeated him, and encamped west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan then advanced with Zhou Fang into Hunan, sent Yang Ju ahead, shattered Du Tao, and camped west of the city.

sentences.zh: 侃之佐史辭詣王敦曰：「州將陶使君孤根特立，從微至著，忠允之功，所在有效。

translations.literal: Kan's aides submitted a petition to Wang Dun saying: 'The provincial commander Tao, a lone root standing alone, from low to high, loyal and trustworthy merit, wherever stationed has been effective.'
translations.idiomatic: His staff drafted a plea to Wang Dun: "Prefect Tao rose alone from obscurity to prominence; his loyal service has succeeded wherever he was posted."

sentences.zh: 出佐南夏，輔翼劉征南，前遇張昌，後屬陳敏，侃以偏旅，獨當大寇，無征不剋，群醜破滅。

translations.literal: He went out as aide in the southern provinces, winged Liu the southern expeditionary general; first encountered Zhang Chang, afterward faced Chen Min; Kan with a partial force alone opposed great bandits; without a campaign he did not conquer; the mass of villains was destroyed and extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Great River he served under General Liu of the southern expedition, first against Zhang Chang, then against Chen Min; leading only a modest column he repeatedly took the field against major rebels, never fought a battle he did not win, and shattered their hosts completely.

sentences.zh: 近者王如亂北，杜弢跨南，二征奔走，一州星馳，其餘郡縣，所在土崩。

translations.literal: Recently Wang Ru troubled the north, Du Tao spanned the south; the two expeditionary generals fled, one province ran like stars; the remaining commanderies and counties everywhere collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Lately Wang Ru has ravaged the north while Du Tao straddles the south; two field armies have fled and the whole province has scattered; commandery after commandery has crumbled.

sentences.zh: 侃招攜以禮，懷遠以德，子來之眾，前後累至。

translations.literal: Kan by ritual summoned and led the distant, by virtue embraced the far; crowds who came as children, before and after repeatedly arrived.
translations.idiomatic: With courtesy he drew wavering bands to his side and with kindness he won the distant; refugees flocked to him in waves.

sentences.zh: 奉承指授，獨守危厄，人往不動，人離不散。

translations.literal: Receiving and carrying out finger-point orders, alone guarded peril; when men went he did not move, when men left he did not scatter.
translations.idiomatic: He obeyed every directive, held a crumbling line alone, and his men neither wavered when others advanced nor broke when others fled.

sentences.zh: 往年董督，徑造湘城，志陵雲霄，神機獨斷。

translations.literal: In former years as superintendent he went straight to Xiang region; his aim overtopped the clouds; divine planning alone decided.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year, as overall commander, he drove deep into Hunan with ambition touching the sky and plans taken solely in his own tent.

sentences.zh: 徒以軍少糧懸，不果獻捷。

translations.literal: Only because the army was few and grain hung suspended, he could not in the end present victory.
translations.idiomatic: He would have offered a victory memorial sooner had his troops not been starved of numbers and supplies.

sentences.zh: 然杜弢懾懼，來還夏口，未經信宿，建平流人迎賊俱叛。

translations.literal: Yet Du Tao was frightened, came back to Xiakou; not yet two nights passed when Jianping displaced persons welcomed the bandits and all rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Du Tao flinched and withdrew to Xiakou, yet within a night or two the refugee settlers of Jianping went over to the rebels en masse.

sentences.zh: 侃即回軍溯流，芟夷丑類，至使西門不鍵，華圻無虞者，侃之功也。

translations.literal: Kan immediately turned the army and went upstream, mowed down the vile sort, reaching the point that the western gate needed no bolt and Huaji had no worry—this was Kan's merit.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan swung his fleet upriver, scoured out the traitors, and kept the western approaches open and the Huaji sector safe—that was his doing.

sentences.zh: 明將軍湣此荊楚，救命塗炭，使侃統領窮殘之餘，寒者衣之，饑者食之，比屋相慶，有若挾纊。

translations.literal: The enlightened general pitied this Jing and Chu, saved lives from mud and charcoal, caused Kan to command the remnants of the exhausted and ruined, clothed those who were cold, fed those who were hungry; house to house mutually celebrated as if clutching silk floss.
translations.idiomatic: You pitied the people of Jing and Chu, snatched them from ruin, and let Tao Kan lead their broken remnants, clothing the freezing and feeding the starving until every household rejoiced as though wrapped in new silk.

sentences.zh: 江濱孤危，地非重險，非可單軍獨能保固，故移就高莋，以避其沖。

translations.literal: The Yangtrench stood lone and perilous; the ground was not layered defences; not possible for a single army alone to be able to protect and solidify; therefore moved to high Zuo to avoid its impact.
translations.idiomatic: The riverbank was exposed ground, not a fortress a lone corps could hold, so he shifted to higher ground at Zuo to escape the enemy's thrust.

sentences.zh: 賊輕易先至，大眾在後，侃距戰經日，殺其名帥。

translations.literal: The bandits lightly and easily arrived first; the great mass was behind; Kan resisted battle for successive days, killed their famous commanders.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard struck lightly while the main body lagged; Tao Kan held them for days and cut down their chief officers.

sentences.zh: 賊尋犬羊相結，並力來攻，侃以忠臣之節，義無退顧，被堅執銳，身當戎行，將士奮擊，莫不用命。

translations.literal: The bandits soon dog-and-sheep knotted together, combined strength came to attack; Kan by a loyal minister's integrity, in righteousness had no retreat or looking back, donned armour grasped sharpness, personally took the battle line; generals and soldiers struck with vigour, none did not use orders.
translations.idiomatic: Then the rabble swarmed as dogs and sheep in a pack; Tao Kan, bound by a loyal minister's duty, had nowhere to retreat. Armored and spear in hand, he took the front rank and his men struck with such fury that every order was obeyed.

sentences.zh: 當時死者不可勝數。

translations.literal: At that time the dead could not be counted for victory.
translations.idiomatic: The dead on that field were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 賊眾參伍，更息更戰。

translations.literal: The bandit host intermingled in threes and fives, rested in turns and fought in turns.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy rotated fresh bands in and out of the fight.

sentences.zh: 侃以孤軍一隊，力不獨禦，量宜取全，以俟後舉。

translations.literal: Kan by one lone army column, strength could not alone resist, measured what was fitting to preserve completeness, to await later raising.
translations.idiomatic: With a single isolated column he could not hold forever; he withdrew on sound judgment to preserve his force for another day.

sentences.zh: 而主者責侃，重加黜削。

translations.literal: Yet the responsible authority blamed Kan, heavily added dismissal and reduction.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his superiors blamed Tao Kan and stripped him of rank.

sentences.zh: 侃性謙沖，功成身退，今奉還所受，唯恐稽遲。

translations.literal: Kan's nature is modest yielding; merit accomplished body retires; now respectfully returns what was received, only fearing delay.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan is by nature modest: when the work is done he steps back. He now returns his commission without delay.

sentences.zh: 然某等區區，實恐理失於內，事敗於外，豪厘之差，將致千里，使荊蠻乖離，西嵎不守，脣亡齒寒，侵逼無限也。

translations.literal: Yet we and others in petty earnest truly fear principle failing within, affairs failing without; a hair's breadth error will lead to a thousand li; causing Jing Man to rebel and separate, the western corner not guarded, lips gone teeth cold, encroachment without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Yet we fear that a hair's breadth of injustice within the court will undo everything without: the tribes of Jing would split away, the western flank would gape, and the old proverb—lips lost, teeth chilled—would bring endless invasion.

sentences.zh: 」敦於是奏復侃官。

translations.literal: Dun thereupon memorialized restoring Kan's office.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun thereupon memorialized for Tao Kan's restoration.

sentences.zh: 韜將王貢精卒三千，出武陵江，誘五溪夷，以舟師斷官運，徑向武昌。

translations.literal: Tao's general Wang Gong with picked soldiers three thousand, went out the Wuling River, enticed the five-stream barbarians, by boat troops cut official transport, went straight toward Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Du Tao's general Wang Gong took three thousand picked men down the Wuling waterway, rallied the Five Streams tribes, cut the government supply line by river, and struck straight for Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 侃使鄭攀及伏波將軍陶延夜趣巴陵，潛師掩其不備，大破之，斬千餘級，降萬餘口。

translations.literal: Kan sent Zheng Pan and General Who Calms the Waves Tao Yan by night hastened to Baling, hid troops and struck them unprepared, greatly defeated them, beheaded more than a thousand grades, surrendered more than ten thousand mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan sent Zheng Pan and Tao Yan, general who calms the waves, on a night march to Baling, caught them unprepared, routed them, took more than a thousand heads, and accepted the surrender of over ten thousand people.

sentences.zh: 貢遁還湘城。

translations.literal: Gong fled back to Xiang city.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong fled back to the Xiang fort.

sentences.zh: 賊中離阻，杜弢遂疑張奕而殺之，眾情益懼，降者滋多。

translations.literal: Within the bandits separation and obstruction; Du Tao thereupon suspected Zhang Yi and killed him; the host's feelings increased fear; those who surrendered daily became more.
translations.idiomatic: Dissension spread through the rebel ranks until Du Tao distrusted Zhang Yi and executed him; morale collapsed and surrenders multiplied.

sentences.zh: 王貢復挑戰，侃遙謂之曰：「杜弢為益州吏，盜用庫錢，父死不奔喪。

translations.literal: Wang Gong again challenged battle; Kan from afar said to him: 'Du Tao was a clerk in Yizhou, stole and used treasury money, when his father died did not rush mourning.'
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Gong offered battle again, Tao Kan shouted across the lines that Du Tao had embezzled public funds as a Yizhou clerk and had failed to observe mourning for his own father.

sentences.zh: 卿本佳人，何為隨之也？

translations.literal: You are originally a fine man; why do you follow him?
translations.idiomatic: You were born a gentleman—why follow such a man?

sentences.zh: 天下寧有白頭賊乎！

translations.literal: Under heaven is there surely a white-haired bandit!
translations.idiomatic: There are no grey-haired bandits under heaven—think what that means for you!

sentences.zh: 」貢初橫腳馬上，侃言訖，貢斂容下腳，辭色甚順。

translations.literal: Gong at first stretched his legs on the horse; when Kan's words ended, Gong composed his face and lowered his legs; words and color were very compliant.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong had been lounging arrogantly in the saddle; when Tao Kan finished, he straightened up, swung down from his mount, and answered meekly.

sentences.zh: 侃知其可動，復令諭之，截髮為信，貢遂來降。
