translations.literal: Kan knew he could be moved, again ordered persuading him, cut hair as pledge; Gong then came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the appeal had struck home, Tao Kan sent further word and cut off his own hair as a pledge of good faith; Wang Gong then capitulated.

sentences.zh: 而韜敗走。

translations.literal: And Tao fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Du Tao broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 進克長沙，獲其將毛寶、高寶、梁堪而還。

translations.literal: Advanced and took Changsha, captured their generals Mao Bao, Gao Bao, Liang Kan and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on, seized Changsha, captured the enemy generals Mao Bao, Gao Bao, and Liang Kan, and marched home.

sentences.zh: 王敦深忌侃功。

translations.literal: Wang Dun deeply envied Kan's merit.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun deeply resented Tao Kan's fame.

sentences.zh: 將還江陵，欲詣敦別，皇甫方回及硃伺等諫，以為不可。

translations.literal: About to return to Jiangling, wished to visit Dun to bid farewell; Huangfu Fanghui and Zhu Si and others remonstrated, deeming it impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: As he prepared to return to Jiangling he meant to call on Wang Dun to say farewell, but Huangfu Fanghui, Zhu Si, and others urged him not to go.

sentences.zh: 侃不從。

translations.literal: Kan did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 敦果留侃不遣，左轉廣州刺史、平越中郎將，以王廣為荊州。

translations.literal: Dun indeed detained Kan and did not send him away, turned left to Inspector of Guang province and Colonel Who Pacifies the Yue, by Wang Guang as Jing province.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun kept him, refused his return, demoted him to inspector of Guangzhou and colonel who pacifies the Yue while appointing Wang Guang over Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 侃之佐吏將士詣敦請留侃。

translations.literal: Kan's aides, generals, and soldiers went to Dun requesting to retain Kan.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan's staff officers and troops went to Wang Dun begging him to let their commander stay.

sentences.zh: 敦怒，不許。

translations.literal: Dun was angry and did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun angrily refused.

sentences.zh: 侃將鄭攀、蘇溫、馬俊等不欲南行，遂西迎杜曾以距暠。

translations.literal: Kan's generals Zheng Pan, Su Wen, Ma Jun and others did not wish to go south, then went west to welcome Du Zeng to resist Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Zheng Pan, Su Wen, and Ma Jun, unwilling to march south, turned west to bring in Du Zeng against Wang Guang.

sentences.zh: 敦意攀承侃風旨，被甲持矛，將殺侃，出而復回者數四。

translations.literal: Dun suspected Pan carried Kan's secret order, donned armour grasped spear, was about to kill Kan, went out and returned again four times.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun thought Zheng Pan acted on Tao Kan's orders, armed himself with spear, and paced outside Tao Kan's quarters four times, poised to kill him.

sentences.zh: 侃正色曰：「使君之雄斷，當裁天下，何此不決乎！

translations.literal: Kan with stern color said: 'The envoy's heroic decision ought to regulate all under heaven; how is this not decided!'
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan said coldly, "If you are bold enough to rule the realm, be bold enough to settle this one point."

sentences.zh: 」因起如廁。

translations.literal: Thereupon rose as if to the privy.
translations.idiomatic: He rose as if to relieve himself.

sentences.zh: 諮議參軍梅陶、長史陳頒言於敦曰：「周訪與侃親姻，如左右手，安有斷人左手而右手不應者乎！

translations.literal: Consultation-adjutant Mei Tao and chief clerk Chen Ban spoke to Dun: 'Zhou Fang and Kan are close kin by marriage like left and right hands; how can there be cutting a man's left hand and the right hand not responding!'
translations.idiomatic: Mei Tao and chief clerk Chen Ban told Wang Dun, "Zhou Fang and Tao Kan are kin by marriage and move as one—no man chops off his own left hand while the right stays idle."

sentences.zh: 」敦意遂解，於是設盛饌以餞之。

translations.literal: Dun's intent thereupon loosened; then set a lavish feast to send him off.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun relented and laid a sumptuous farewell banquet.

sentences.zh: 侃便夜發。

translations.literal: Kan then set out by night.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan slipped away that same night.

sentences.zh: 敦引其子瞻參軍。

translations.literal: Dun led his son Zhan as adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun kept his son Tao Zhan as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 侃既達豫章，見周訪，流涕曰：「非卿外援，我殆不免！

translations.literal: When Kan had reached Yuzhang, saw Zhou Fang, wept and said: 'If not for your outside aid, I nearly could not escape!'
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Yuzhang and meeting Zhou Fang, Tao Kan wept, "Without your help outside I would not have survived."

sentences.zh: 」侃因進至始興。

translations.literal: Kan thereupon advanced to Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: From there he pressed on to Shixing.

sentences.zh: 先是，廣州人背刺史郭訥，迎長沙人王機為刺史。

translations.literal: Earlier, Guangzhou men turned against Inspector Guo Ne, welcomed Changsha man Wang Ji as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the people of Guangzhou had rebelled against Inspector Guo Ne and invited Wang Ji of Changsha to replace him.

sentences.zh: 機復遣使詣王敦，乞為交州。

translations.literal: Ji again sent envoys to Wang Dun, begging to be Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji sent another plea to Wang Dun asking for Jiaozhou instead.

sentences.zh: 敦從之，而機未發。

translations.literal: Dun followed it, but Ji had not yet set out.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun agreed, yet Wang Ji never moved south.

sentences.zh: 會杜弘據臨賀，因機乞降，勸弘取廣州，弘遂與溫邵及交州秀才劉沈俱謀反。

translations.literal: When Du Hong seized Linhe, through Ji begged to surrender, urged Hong to take Guangzhou; Hong then with Wen Shao and Jiaozhou xiucai Liu Shen together plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong seized Linhe, used Wang Ji's offer of surrender to urge him to seize Guangzhou, and then conspired with Wen Shao and the Jiaozhou scholar Liu Shen.

sentences.zh: 或勸侃且住始興，觀察形勢。

translations.literal: Some urged Kan for the nonce to stay at Shixing and observe the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Some advised Tao Kan to pause at Shixing and watch events.

sentences.zh: 侃不聽，直至廣州。

translations.literal: Kan did not listen, went straight to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He ignored them and marched straight for Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 弘遣使偽降。

translations.literal: Hong sent envoys feigning surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong sent envoys pretending to capitulate.

sentences.zh: 侃知其詐，先於封口起發石車。

translations.literal: Kan knew his deceit, beforehand at Fengkou raised stone-throwing carts.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan saw through the ruse and had stone-throwing engines set up at Fengkou.

sentences.zh: 俄而弘率輕兵而至，知侃有備，乃退。

translations.literal: Soon Hong led light troops and arrived, knew Kan had preparations, then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Hong came up with light forces and found Tao Kan ready, he pulled back.

sentences.zh: 侃追擊破之，執劉沈于小桂。

translations.literal: Kan pursued, struck, defeated them, captured Liu Shen at Xiaogui.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan pursued, routed him, and took Liu Shen at Xiaogui.

sentences.zh: 又遣部將許高討機，斬之，傳首京都。

translations.literal: Also sent subordinate general Xu Gao to attack Ji, beheaded him, transmitted the head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Xu Gao against Wang Ji, executed him, and sent the head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆請乘勝擊溫邵，侃笑曰：「吾威名已著，何事遣兵，但一函紙自足耳。

translations.literal: The generals all requested to ride victory to strike Wen Shao; Kan laughed and said: 'My awe-inspiring name is already established; what matter to dispatch troops—a single letter suffices.'
translations.idiomatic: When his officers begged to pursue Wen Shao, Tao Kan laughed and said, "My name alone will finish it—one letter is enough."

sentences.zh: 」於是下書諭之。

translations.literal: Thereupon issued a document instructing them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a written summons instead.

sentences.zh: 邵懼而走，追獲於始興。

translations.literal: Shao feared and fled, was pursued and captured at Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Shao fled in panic and was run down at Shixing.

sentences.zh: 以功封柴桑侯，食邑四千戶。

translations.literal: By merit was enfeoffed marquis of Chaisang, fief of four thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For these services he was enfeoffed as marquis of Chaisang with a fief of four thousand households.

sentences.zh: 侃在州無事，輒朝運百甓於齋外，暮運於齋內。

translations.literal: Kan in the province had nothing to do, then each morning transported a hundred bricks outside the studio, each evening transported them inside the studio.
translations.idiomatic: With little to do in Guangzhou he hauled a hundred bricks every morning from his office to the yard and back inside each evening.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，答曰：「吾方致力中原，過爾優逸，恐不堪事。

translations.literal: People asked the reason; he replied: 'I am about to exert strength on the central plain; passing thus in ease and comfort, I fear not bearing affairs.'
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he said, "I mean to strike north again; if I grow soft in comfort I will not endure the task."

sentences.zh: 」其勵志勤力，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His encouraging ambition and diligent strength were all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His self-discipline was of that stamp throughout.

sentences.zh: 太興初，進號平南將軍，尋加都督交州軍事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taixing, advanced title General Who Pacifies the South, soon added area commander for Jiao province military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taixing era he was promoted general who pacifies the south and soon given command over Jiaozhou as well.

sentences.zh: 及王敦舉兵反，詔侃以本官領江州刺史，尋轉都督、湘州刺史。

translations.literal: When Wang Dun raised troops in rebellion, an edict ordered Kan with original office to hold Jiangzhou Inspector, soon transferred area commander and Xiangzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun rebelled, an edict named Tao Kan inspector of Jiangzhou in addition to his standing titles, then shifted him to area commander and inspector of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 敦得志，上侃復本職，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Dun achieved his aim, memorialized Kan restored to original office, added cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Dun had his way he memorialized Tao Kan back to his former post with the added title cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 時交州刺史王諒為賊梁碩所陷，侃遣將高寶進擊平之。

translations.literal: At that time Jiaozhou Inspector Wang Liang was by bandit Liang Shuo trapped; Kan sent general Gao Bao to attack and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: When Inspector Wang Liang of Jiaozhou fell to the rebel Liang Shuo, Tao Kan sent Gao Bao to crush the uprising.

sentences.zh: 以侃領交州刺史。

translations.literal: By Kan holding Jiaozhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan was concurrently named inspector of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 錄前後功，封次子夏為都亭侯，進號征南大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Recording former and later merit, enfeoffed second son Xia as village marquis of Douting, advanced title General Who Conquers the South, establishment of office equal to the three excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: His accumulated honors won his second son, Tao Xia, a village marquisate at Douting and himself the titles general who conquers the south with an independent headquarters equated to the three senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 及王敦平，遷都督荊、雍、益、梁州諸軍事，領護南蠻校尉、征西大將軍、荊州刺史，余如故。

translations.literal: When Wang Dun was pacified, was moved area commander for Jing, Yong, Yi, and Liang military affairs, concurrently Colonel of the Southern Man, General Who Conquers the West, Inspector of Jing province, remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Dun's fall he became area commander over Jing, Yong, Yi, and Liang, kept the colonelcy of the southern tribes, and was named general who conquers the west and inspector of Jingzhou, his other titles unchanged.

sentences.zh: 楚郢士女莫不相慶。

translations.literal: Chu and Ying gentry and women none did not mutually celebrate.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry and commoners across Chu and Ying rejoiced together.

sentences.zh: 侃性聰敏，勤於吏職，恭而近禮，愛好人倫。

translations.literal: Kan's nature was clever and keen, diligent in clerk duty, respectful and close to ritual, loved human relationships.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan was quick-witted, tireless in administrative detail, courteous and observant of ritual, and genuinely fond of cultivating men of talent.

sentences.zh: 終日斂膝危坐，閫外多事，千緒萬端，罔有遺漏。

translations.literal: All day drew up knees and sat dangerously; beyond the camp many affairs, thousand threads ten thousand ends, none were missed.
translations.idiomatic: He sat bolt upright from dawn to dusk; though business poured in from every quarter, nothing slipped through his fingers.

sentences.zh: 遠近書疏，莫不手答，筆翰如流，未嘗壅滯。

translations.literal: Near and far letters and memorials, none he did not personally answer; brush and ink like flowing, never blocked or stuck.
translations.idiomatic: He answered every letter himself, his brush never faltering.

sentences.zh: 引接疏遠，門無停客。

translations.literal: He drew in the distant; at the gate no stopping guests.
translations.idiomatic: He welcomed even humble callers, so that his gate was never idle.

sentences.zh: 常語人曰：「大禹聖者，乃惜寸陰，至於眾人，當惜分陰，豈可逸遊荒醉，生無益于時，死無聞於後，是自棄也。

translations.literal: He often told people: 'Great Yu was a sage, yet treasured each inch of shadow; as for the multitude, ought to treasure each fraction of shadow; how can one roam in leisure and wild drunkenness—living without benefit to the times, dying without hearing behind—this is self-abandonment.'
translations.idiomatic: He used to say, "Even the sage-king Yu cherished every inch of daylight; common men should cherish every minute. How can we idle and drunk—useless in life, forgotten in death—and not call it throwing ourselves away?"

sentences.zh: 」諸參佐或以談戲廢事者，乃命取其酒器、蒱博之具，悉投之于江，吏將則加鞭撲，曰：「樗蒱者，牧豬奴戲耳！

translations.literal: His various adjutants some by talk and play wasted affairs; then he ordered taking their wine vessels and gambling tools, all threw them into the river; to clerks and generals then added whipping, saying: 'Chupu is a swineherd's game!'
translations.idiomatic: When aides wasted office hours in chatter and games, he had their wine cups and dice boards seized and flung into the river, and clerks who offended were flogged, saying, "Dice is a game fit for pig-herds."

sentences.zh: 《老》《莊》浮華，非先王之法言，不可行也。

translations.literal: Laozi and Zhuangzi are vain flourish, not the model words of former kings; may not be practiced.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist texts of Laozi and Zhuangzi are idle ornament, not the teaching of the ancient kings, and have no place in my administration.

sentences.zh: 君子當正其衣冠，攝其威儀，何有亂頭養望自謂宏達邪！

translations.literal: A gentleman ought to straighten his cap and robes, gather his awe-inspiring deportment; how can there be disheveled head nurturing reputation, calling oneself grand penetration!
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman sets his cap straight and composes his bearing—how dare we muss our hair for reputation and pretend to lofty ease?

sentences.zh: 」有奉饋者，皆問其所由。

translations.literal: When there were those who brought gifts, all asked whence they came.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever gifts arrived he asked how they had been obtained.

sentences.zh: 若力作所致，雖微必喜，慰賜參倍；

translations.literal: If by labor strength brought about, although slight he was surely pleased, consoled and rewarded several-fold;
translations.idiomatic: If they came from honest toil, however small the gift he accepted it gladly and returned double thanks.

sentences.zh: 若非理得之，則切厲訶辱，還其所饋。

translations.literal: If by unrighteous principle obtained, then sharply scolded and insulted, returned what was gifted.
translations.idiomatic: If they came by crooked means he cursed the giver and sent the goods back.

sentences.zh: 嘗出遊，見人持一把未熟稻，侃問：「用此何為？

translations.literal: Once on going out he saw a man holding a handful of unripe rice; Kan asked: 'Using this for what?'
translations.idiomatic: Once on an outing he saw someone clutching a handful of unripe grain and demanded to know its purpose.

sentences.zh: 」人云：「行道所見，聊取之耳。

translations.literal: The man said: 'Walking on the road what I saw, casually took it.'
translations.idiomatic: The man said he had picked it casually along the road.

sentences.zh: 」侃大怒曰：「汝既不田，而戲賊人稻！

translations.literal: Kan greatly angry said: 'You neither plough fields, yet play at thieving people's rice!'
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan roared, "You do not farm, yet you steal the farmers' grain for sport!"

sentences.zh: 」執而鞭之。

translations.literal: Seized him and whipped him.
translations.idiomatic: He had the man seized and flogged.

sentences.zh: 是以百姓勤于農殖，家給人足。

translations.literal: Therefore the hundred surnames were diligent in farming and breeding; households supplied and people sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: From that day the people labored hard in the fields until every home had enough.

sentences.zh: 時造船，木屑及竹頭悉令舉掌之，咸不解所以。

translations.literal: At that time building ships, wood shavings and bamboo ends he ordered all lifted and kept; all did not understand the reason.
translations.idiomatic: When ships were built he ordered every scrap of wood and bamboo tip saved, though no one understood why.

sentences.zh: 後正會，積雪始晴，聽事前餘雪猶濕，於是以屑布地。

translations.literal: Later at the new-year gathering, accumulated snow had just cleared; before the audience hall remaining snow was still wet; thereupon used shavings to spread the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at the new-year levee after a heavy snow, he carpeted the slick hall with those saved shavings.

sentences.zh: 及桓溫伐蜀，又以侃所貯竹頭作丁裝船。

translations.literal: When Huan Wen attacked Shu, again used what Kan had stored bamboo ends to make nail-fitted ships.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Wen campaigned into Shu he used Tao Kan's hoarded bamboo tips to fit out the fleet.

sentences.zh: 其綜理微密，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His overall management minute and close were all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His eye for detail ran to that level in everything.

sentences.zh: 暨蘇峻作逆，京都不守，侃子瞻為賊所害，平南將軍溫嶠要侃同赴朝廷。

translations.literal: When Su Jun rebelled, the capital did not hold; Kan's son Zhan was by bandits harmed; General Who Pacifies the South Wen Qiao invited Kan together to go to the court.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Jun seized the capital and killed his son Tao Zhan, Wen Qiao, general who pacifies the south, begged Tao Kan to march to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 初，明帝崩，侃不在顧命之列，深以為恨，答嶠曰：「吾疆場外將，不敢越局。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Ming died, Kan was not in the testamentary commission list, deeply took it as resentment, answered Qiao: 'I am a border general beyond the frontier, dare not overstep my office.'
translations.idiomatic: Because he had been left off Emperor Ming's deathbed council, Tao Kan nursed a grudge and at first answered Wen Qiao, "I am only a frontier commander and dare not overstep my charge."

sentences.zh: 」嶠固請之，因推為盟主。

translations.literal: Qiao firmly requested him, thereby pushed him as covenant lord.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qiao pressed him until he accepted leadership of the alliance.

sentences.zh: 侃乃遣督護龔登率眾赴嶠，而又追回。

translations.literal: Kan then sent protector Gong Deng leading masses to go to Qiao, yet again recalled them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Gong Deng to Wen Qiao, then countermanded the order.

sentences.zh: 嶠以峻殺其子，重遣書以激怒之。

translations.literal: Qiao because Jun killed his son, again sent letters to enrage him.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qiao wrote again, playing on Su Jun's murder of Tao Zhan to sting him into action.

sentences.zh: 侃妻龔氏亦固勸自行。

translations.literal: Kan's wife Lady Gong also firmly urged him to go himself.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Gong, his wife, also urged him to take the field in person.

sentences.zh: 於是便戎服登舟，星言兼邁，瞻喪至不臨。

translations.literal: Thereupon in martial garboard boarded boats, by star speech doubled march, when Zhan's mourning arrived did not attend.
translations.idiomatic: He donned armor, embarked, and raced by night without pausing even when his son's funeral train arrived.

sentences.zh: 五月，與溫嶠、庾亮等俱會石頭。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, together with Wen Qiao, Yu Liang, and others all met at Stone Fort.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he joined Wen Qiao, Yu Liang, and the others at Stone Fort.

sentences.zh: 諸軍即欲決戰，侃以賊盛，不可爭鋒，當以歲月智計擒之。

translations.literal: The various armies at once wished decisive battle; Kan because the bandits were abundant, could not contend sharp points, ought by years and months with wisdom and plan capture them.
translations.idiomatic: The allies wanted a pitched battle, but Tao Kan held that the rebels were too strong for a frontal clash and must be worn down over time.

sentences.zh: 累戰無功，諸將請于查浦築壘。

translations.literal: Repeated battles without achievement; the generals requested at Zhapu to build ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: After several indecisive fights his officers asked to throw up earthworks at Zhapu.

sentences.zh: 監軍部將李根建議，請立白石壘。

translations.literal: Army supervisor subordinate general Li Gen proposed a plan, requesting to erect White Stone rampart.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gen, a general under the army supervisor, urged him to fortify the White Stone height.

sentences.zh: 侃不從，曰：「若壘不成，卿當坐之。

translations.literal: Kan did not follow, saying: 'If the rampart is not completed, you will sit for it.'
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan refused at first, warning Li Gen, "If the work fails, you will answer for it."

sentences.zh: 」根曰：「查浦地下，又在水南，唯白石峻極險固，可容數千人，賊來攻不便，滅賊之術也。

translations.literal: Gen said: 'Zhapu lies low underground, again on the water's south; only White Stone is steep and extreme peril and solid, can hold several thousand men; when bandits come to attack it is not convenient; it is the art of destroying bandits.'
translations.idiomatic: Li Gen replied that Zhapu was marshy and south of the river, whereas White Stone was steep, defensible, and could shelter thousands while hampering any assault—the sure way to destroy the enemy.

sentences.zh: 」侃笑曰：「卿良將也。

translations.literal: Kan laughed and said: 'You are a fine general.'
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan laughed and said, "You are a good soldier."

sentences.zh: 」乃從根謀，夜修曉訖。

translations.literal: Thereupon followed Gen's plan; by night built, by dawn finished.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted Li Gen's plan; the wall rose overnight and stood complete at dawn.

sentences.zh: 賊見壘大驚。

translations.literal: The bandits saw the rampart and greatly marveled.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels gaped at the new fortress.

sentences.zh: 賊攻大業壘，侃將救之，長史殷羨曰：「若遣救大業，步戰不如峻，則大事去矣。

translations.literal: The bandits attacked the Daye rampart; Kan was about to rescue it; chief clerk Yin Xian said: 'If you send relief to Daye, in foot battle you will not match Jun, then the great affair is gone.'
translations.idiomatic: When Su Jun stormed the Daye fort Tao Kan started to relieve it, but Yin Xian warned that splitting the army for a foot battle Su Jun would win would lose everything.

sentences.zh: 但當急攻石頭，峻必救之，而大業自解。

translations.literal: Only ought urgently to attack Stone Fort; Jun must rescue it, and Daye of itself will be loosened.
translations.idiomatic: Strike Stone Fort with everything you have, he urged, and Su Jun would abandon Daye to save his base.

sentences.zh: 」侃又從羨言。

translations.literal: Kan again followed Xian's words.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan took Yin Xian's advice.

sentences.zh: 峻果棄大業而救石頭。

translations.literal: Jun indeed abandoned Daye to rescue Stone Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun did pull out of Daye to rescue Stone Fort.

sentences.zh: 諸軍與峻戰陳陵東，侃督護竟陵太守李陽部將彭世斬峻於陣，賊眾大潰。

translations.literal: The various armies with Jun battled east of Chenling; Kan's protector Jingling prefect Li Yang's subordinate Peng Shi beheaded Jun in the formation; the bandit host greatly collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: East of Chenling the allies met Su Jun in battle; Peng Shi, an officer under Tao Kan's protector Li Yang, prefect of Jingling, cut Su Jun down on the field and the rebel army collapsed.

sentences.zh: 峻弟逸復聚眾。

translations.literal: Jun's younger brother Yi again gathered masses.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun's brother Su Yi rallied the remnants.

sentences.zh: 侃與諸軍斬逸於石頭。

translations.literal: Kan with the various armies beheaded Yi at Stone Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan and the allied hosts executed Su Yi at Stone Fort.

sentences.zh: 初，庾亮少有高名，以明穆皇后之兄受顧命之重，蘇峻之禍，職亮是由。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yu Liang in youth had a high name, by being the Bright-Modest empress's elder brother received the testamentary commission's weight; the Su Jun disaster, the duty lay with Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang had won fame while young and, as brother of Empress Mingmu, bore heavy deathbed trust; many blamed him for the Su Jun disaster.

sentences.zh: 及石頭平，懼侃致討，亮用溫嶠謀，詣侃拜謝。

translations.literal: When Stone Fort was pacified, fearing Kan would arrive in punishment, Liang used Wen Qiao's plan, went to Kan to bow in apology.
translations.idiomatic: After Stone Fort fell Yu Liang feared Tao Kan's vengeance and, on Wen Qiao's advice, came to offer a humble apology.

sentences.zh: 侃遽止之，曰：「庾元規乃拜陶士行邪！

translations.literal: Kan hastily stopped him, saying: 'Yu Yuangui is actually bowing to Tao Shixing!'
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan stopped him short, exclaiming, "Is Yu Yuangui really going to bow to Tao Shixing?"

sentences.zh: 」王導入石頭城，令取故節，侃笑曰：「蘇武節似不如是！

translations.literal: Wang Dao entered Stone Fort city, ordered to take the old staff; Kan laughed and said: 'Su Wu's staff seems not like this!'
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dao entered Stone Fort and asked for the old credential staff, Tao Kan laughed, "Su Wu's shepherd's staff did not look like that."

sentences.zh: 」導有慚色，使人屏之。

translations.literal: Dao had a shameful color, ordered men to screen it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao flushed and had the matter hushed up.

sentences.zh: 侃旋江陵，尋以為侍中、太尉，加羽葆鼓吹，改封長沙郡公，邑三千戶，賜絹八千匹，加都督交、廣、寧七州軍事。

translations.literal: Kan returned to Jiangling; soon by him as palace attendant, grand commandant, added feather canopy and band, changed enfeoffment to duke of Changsha commandery, fief three thousand households, granted silk eight thousand bolts, added area commander for Jiao, Guang, and Ning seven provinces' military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew to Jiangling, then was named palace attendant and grand commandant with full honors, re-enfeoffed as duke of Changsha with three thousand households and eight thousand bolts of silk, and made area commander over seven provinces including Jiao and Guang.

sentences.zh: 以江陵偏遠，移鎮巴陵。

translations.literal: Because Jiangling was remote on the side, moved garrison to Baling.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Jiangling too far upriver, he shifted his headquarters to Baling.

sentences.zh: 遣諮議參軍張誕討五溪夷，降之。

translations.literal: Sent consultation-adjutant Zhang Dan to attack the five-stream barbarians and made them surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhang Dan against the Five Streams tribes and accepted their surrender.

sentences.zh: 屬後將軍郭默矯詔襲殺平南將軍劉胤，輒領江州。

translations.literal: It happened that Rear General Guo Mo forged an edict, raided and killed General Who Pacifies the South Liu Yin, then held Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Rear General Guo Mo used a forged decree to murder Liu Yin, general who pacifies the south, and seized Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 侃聞之曰：「此必詐也。

translations.literal: When Kan heard it he said: 'This must be a fraud.'
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan said at once, "This cannot be genuine."

sentences.zh: 」遣將軍宋夏、陳修率兵據湓口，侃以大軍繼進。

translations.literal: Sent generals Song Xia and Chen Xiu to lead troops and hold Penkou; Kan with the great army followed and advanced.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Song Xia and Chen Xiu to seal Penkou and followed with the main army.

sentences.zh: 默遣使送妓婢絹百匹，寫中詔呈侃。

translations.literal: Mo sent envoys delivering singing girls, concubines, and a hundred bolts of silk, writing an inner edict to present to Kan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Mo sent singing girls, maids, a hundred bolts of silk, and a counterfeit palace edict.

sentences.zh: 參佐多諫曰：「默不被詔，豈敢為此事。

translations.literal: Adjutants many remonstrated saying: 'Mo did not receive an edict; how dare he do this affair.'
translations.idiomatic: Most of his staff urged caution: "Without an imperial order Guo Mo would never dare such a thing."

sentences.zh: 若進軍，宜待詔報。

translations.literal: If advancing the army, ought to await edict reply.'
translations.idiomatic: They said the march should wait on a court reply.

sentences.zh: 」侃厲色曰：「國家年小，不出胸懷。

translations.literal: Kan with stern color said: 'The state is young in years, not yet out of the breast;'
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan answered sharply, "The throne is still held by a child who has not left the nursery."

sentences.zh: 且劉胤為朝廷所禮，雖方任非才，何緣猥加極刑！

translations.literal: Moreover Liu Yin was treated with courtesy by the court; although regional appointment was not matched to talent, how could there be reason to apply extreme punishment vulgarly!'
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Liu Yin was honored at court; even if his appointment was a poor fit, nothing justified murdering him out of hand.

sentences.zh: 郭默虓勇，所在暴掠，以大難新除，威網寬簡，欲因隙會騁其從橫耳。

translations.literal: Guo Mo is fierce brave; wherever located he violently plunders; because the great disaster was newly removed, awe and nets are wide and simple, he wishes by gap and chance to gallop his horizontal and vertical course.'
translations.idiomatic: Guo Mo is a brutal marauder who exploits every loosening of the law after the recent wars to run wild.

sentences.zh: 」發使上表討默。

translations.literal: Dispatched envoys upward memorializing to attack Mo.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a memorial demanding permission to crush Guo Mo.

sentences.zh: 與王導書曰：「郭默殺方州，即用為方州；

translations.literal: Writing to Wang Dao he said: 'Guo Mo killed a regional inspector, then immediately was made regional inspector;'
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Wang Dao, "Guo Mo murders a provincial inspector and is rewarded with a province—"

sentences.zh: 害宰相，便為宰相乎？

translations.literal: Kills a chief minister, then becomes chief minister?'
translations.idiomatic: —murders a chief minister and expects to become chief minister?

sentences.zh: 」導答曰：「默居上流之勢，加有船艦成資，故苞含隱忍，使其有地。

translations.literal: Dao answered saying: 'Mo occupies the upper stream's power, plus has boats and ships as completed resources; therefore wrapped and contained, hid and endured, letting him have ground.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao answered that Guo Mo commanded the upper Yangzi and a ready fleet, so the court had temporized rather than provoke him.

sentences.zh: 一月潛嚴，足下軍到，是以得風發相赴，豈非遵養時晦以定大事者邪！

translations.literal: For one month secretly prepared rigorously; when your foot army arrived, therefore was able to sail with the wind and rush to meet him—is this not obeying and nurturing the times' darkness thereby to settle the great affair!'
translations.idiomatic: For a month, he explained, the court had secretly armed itself; now that Tao Kan's host was near they could strike together—was that not "biding the murky hour" to settle the crisis?

sentences.zh: 」侃省書笑曰：「是乃遵養時賊也。

translations.literal: Kan read the letter and laughed saying: 'This is obeying and nurturing the times' bandit.'
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan read the letter and laughed, "That is biding time for the bandit, not for the realm."

sentences.zh: 」侃既至，默將宗侯縛默父子五人及默將張醜詣侃降，侃斬默等。

translations.literal: When Kan arrived, Mo's general Zong Hou bound Mo, his father and sons five persons, and Mo's general Zhang Chou, came to Kan to surrender; Kan beheaded Mo and the others.
translations.idiomatic: As Tao Kan approached, Guo Mo's officer Zong Hou bound Guo Mo, his five sons, and general Zhang Chou and surrendered them; Tao Kan executed Guo Mo and his party.

sentences.zh: 默在中原，數與石勒等戰，賊畏其勇，聞侃討之，兵不血刃而擒也，益畏侃。

translations.literal: Mo in the central plain repeatedly battled with Shi Le and others; bandits feared his courage; hearing Kan attacked him, soldiers did not bloody blades yet captured him; all the more feared Kan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Mo had fought Shi Le repeatedly in the north and terrified other warlords; when Tao Kan moved against him he was taken without a blow being struck, which only deepened their awe of Tao Kan.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻將馮鐵殺侃子，奔于石勒，勒以為戍將。

translations.literal: Su Jun's general Feng Tie killed Kan's son, fled to Shi Le; Le by him made garrison general.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Tie, a general of Su Jun who had killed Tao Kan's son, fled to Shi Le, who made him a frontier commander.

sentences.zh: 侃告勒以故，勒召而殺之。

translations.literal: Kan informed Le of the reason; Le summoned and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan sent word of the blood feud to Shi Le, who summoned Feng Tie and executed him.

sentences.zh: 詔侃都督江州，領刺史，增置左右長史、司馬、從事中郎四人，掾屬十二人。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Kan area commander of Jiangzhou, holding inspector, added left and right chief clerks, marshals, and four adjutants, twelve clerks.
translations.idiomatic: An edict named Tao Kan area commander of Jiangzhou with the inspectorship, enlarged his staff with paired chief clerks, marshals, four senior adjutants, and twelve subordinates.

sentences.zh: 侃旋于巴陵，因移鎮武昌。

translations.literal: Kan returned from Baling, thereupon moved garrison to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to Baling he transferred his headquarters to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 侃命張夔子隱為參軍，范達子珧為湘東太守，辟劉弘曾孫安為掾屬，表論梅陶，凡微時所荷，一餐咸報。

translations.literal: Kan ordered Zhang Kui's son Yin as adjutant, Fan Kui's son Yao as Xiangdong prefect, summoned Liu Hong's great-grandson An as clerk, memorialized discussing Mei Tao; all whom in low times he had borne a single meal from, all he repaid.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Zhang Yin's son to his staff, Fan Kui's son prefect of eastern Xiang, called Liu Hong's descendant Liu An into service, and again lifted up Mei Tao—every man who had once given him a meal he now repaid.

sentences.zh: 遣子斌與南中郎將桓宣西伐樊城，走石勒將郭敬。

translations.literal: Sent son Bin with General of the Center Huan Xuan west to attack Fancheng, routing Shi Le's general Guo Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Tao Bin with Huan Xuan, general of the center, west against Fancheng and drove off Guo Jing, a general of Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 使兄子臻、竟陵太守李陽等共破新野，遂平襄陽。

translations.literal: Caused elder brother's son Zhen, Jingling prefect Li Yang, and others jointly to break Xinye, thereupon pacified Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Tao Zhen and Li Yang, prefect of Jingling, took Xinye together and secured Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 拜大將軍，劍履上殿，入朝不趨，贊拜不名。

translations.literal: Was appointed grand marshal, sword and shoes on hall, entering court not hastening, praise obeisance not naming.
translations.idiomatic: He was named grand marshal with the honors of wearing sword and shoes in audience, entering court without hurrying, and being hailed without his name spoken.

sentences.zh: 上表固讓，曰：「臣非貪於疇昔，而虛讓於今日。

translations.literal: Submitted memorial firmly declining, saying: 'Your subject is not greedy in former days, yet vainly declines today.'
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized a firm refusal: "I do not cling to past glories, yet I must decline what is offered now."

sentences.zh: 事有合于時宜，臣豈敢與陛下有違；

translations.literal: If affairs fit the times' rightness, how dare your subject oppose Your Majesty;'
translations.idiomatic: When the times call for a thing, I would not set myself against Your Majesty;

sentences.zh: 理有益於聖世，臣豈與朝廷作異。

translations.literal: if principle benefits the sage age, how dare your subject differ from the court.'
translations.idiomatic: when principle serves the age, I would not quarrel with the court.

sentences.zh: 臣常欲除諸浮長之事，遣諸虛假之用，非獨臣身而已。

translations.literal: Your subject constantly wished to remove the many floating excess affairs, dispatch the many false usages; not alone your subject's body only.'
translations.idiomatic: I have always wished to cut empty offices and false appointments—not for my sake alone.

sentences.zh: 若臣杖國威靈，梟雄斬勒，則又何以加！

translations.literal: If your subject wields the state's awesome spirit, the fierce chief beheads Le, then what more could be added!'
translations.idiomatic: Were I to wield the imperial majesty and strike down a tyrant like Shi Le, what higher honor could I seek?

sentences.zh: 」咸和七年六月疾篤，又上表遜位曰：

translations.literal: In the sixth month of Xianhe year seven, gravely ill, again submitted memorial yielding position, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the seventh Xianhe year, gravely ill, he submitted another memorial asking to retire, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣少長孤寒，始願有限。

translations.literal: Your subject from youth to age was orphaned and cold; original aspiration had limits.
translations.idiomatic: "From childhood I knew poverty and modest hopes."

sentences.zh: 過蒙聖朝曆世殊恩、陛下睿鑒，寵靈彌泰。

translations.literal: Excessively receiving the sage court's successive generations' special grace, Your Majesty's keen insight, favor and numinous ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Yet reign after reign heaped favor on me, and Your Majesty's discerning eye raised me higher still.

sentences.zh: 有始必終，自古而然。

translations.literal: Having beginning must have end, from antiquity thus.
translations.idiomatic: What begins must end—that has been true since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 臣年垂八十，位極人臣，啟手啟足，當復何恨！

translations.literal: Your subject's years hang toward eighty, rank has reached the limit of human ministers; folding hands folding feet—what further regret!'
translations.idiomatic: I am nearing eighty and have climbed as high as a subject may; when I close my hands in death I shall have no regrets.

sentences.zh: 但以陛下春秋尚富，餘寇不誅，山陵未反，所以憤愾兼懷，不能已已。

translations.literal: Only because Your Majesty's spring and autumn are still rich, remaining bandits are not executed, the imperial tombs are not returned—therefore indignant sorrow fills the breast, unable to stop.'
translations.idiomatic: Only because you are still young, rebels remain, and the imperial tombs lie in enemy hands does grief keep me from rest.

sentences.zh: 臣雖不知命，年時已邁，國恩殊特，賜封長沙，隕越之日，當歸骨國土。

translations.literal: Your subject although does not know fate, years and season already passed; state grace especially special, granted enfeoffment Changsha; on the day of falling beyond, ought to return bones to the state's soil.'
translations.idiomatic: Though I cannot read heaven's will, my years are spent; the grace that made me duke of Changsha means that when I fall I wish my bones returned to that fief.

sentences.zh: 臣父母舊葬，今在尋陽，緣存處亡，無心分違，已勒國臣修遷改之事，刻以來秋，奉迎窀穸，葬事訖，乃告老下籓。

translations.literal: Your subject's father and mother's old burials are now at Xunyang; bound by the living place of the dead, without heart to divide and depart; already ordered the state's clerks to repair removal and change affairs, set for next autumn to welcome the grave, when burial affairs are finished, then will report old age and descend to the princedom.'
translations.idiomatic: My parents lie buried at Xunyang; I cannot bear to leave them; I have ordered my household to prepare their reburial next autumn, after which I meant to retire to my princedom.

sentences.zh: 不圖所患，遂爾綿篤，伏枕感結，情不自勝。

translations.literal: Not expecting the illness suffered, thus became prolonged and grave; lying on the pillow sorrow knots, feeling cannot overcome itself.'
translations.idiomatic: Instead my sickness has deepened; prostrate with grief I can scarcely master myself.

sentences.zh: 臣間者猶為犬馬之齒尚可小延，欲為陛下西平李雄，北吞石季龍，是以遣毌丘奧於巴東，授桓宣於襄陽。

translations.literal: Your subject recently still thought dog-and-horse years could still slightly extend, wished for Your Majesty west to pacify Li Xiong, north to swallow Shi Jilong; therefore sent Wuqiu Ao to Badong, appointed Huan Xuan at Xiangyang.'
translations.idiomatic: Until lately I thought I might linger yet and westward crush Li Xiong and northward swallow Shi Hu—that is why I posted Wuqiu Ao in Badong and Huan Xuan at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 良圖未敘，於此長乖！

translations.literal: Good plans not yet narrated, here forever part!'
translations.idiomatic: Those plans are unfinished, and I must leave them forever.

sentences.zh: 此方之任，內外之要，願陛下速選臣代使，必得良才，奉宣王猷，遵成臣志，則臣死之日猶生之年。

translations.literal: This side's duties, inner and outer essentials—wish Your Majesty quickly to select your subject's replacement, must obtain fine talent, to proclaim the royal pattern, to follow and complete your subject's intent, then on the day your subject dies is still like the year of life.'
translations.idiomatic: I beg you quickly to name a successor for this command, a worthy man who can carry out your design, so that my death may still serve the living.

sentences.zh: 陛下雖聖姿天縱，英奇日新，方事之殷，當賴群俊。

translations.literal: Although Your Majesty by sage bearing heaven's overflow, heroic wonder daily renews, just as affairs are abundant, ought to rely on the host of excellence.'
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Majesty's talent overflows heaven and grows daily, these pressing tasks demand many able ministers.

sentences.zh: 司徒導鑒識經遠，光輔三世；

translations.literal: Minister Dao's insight is classic and far-reaching, brilliantly assisting three generations;'
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wang Dao sees deep and steady and has aided three reigns;

sentences.zh: 司空鑒簡素貞正，內外惟允；

translations.literal: Minister Jian is plain, upright, and true, inner and outer alike trusted;'
translations.idiomatic: Minister Yu Jian is plain, loyal, and trusted within and without;

sentences.zh: 平西將軍亮雅量詳明，器用周時，即陛下之周召也。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the West Liang's elegant measure is detailed and clear, implements are timely—he is Your Majesty's Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao.'
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang, general who pacifies the west, is calm, clear, and timely—the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao at your side.

sentences.zh: 獻替疇諮，敷融政道，地平天成，四海幸賴。

translations.literal: Presenting and removing in counsel, spreading and harmonizing government way, earth level heaven completed, within the four seas fortunately rely.'
translations.idiomatic: Let them counsel you freely and smooth the government until heaven and earth are level and the realm rests secure.

sentences.zh: 謹遣左長史殷羨奉送所假節麾、幢曲蓋、侍中貂蟬、太尉章、荊江州刺史印傳啟戟。

translations.literal: Respectfully sending left chief clerk Yin Xian to deliver the lent staff, banner, curved canopy, palace attendant's sable cicada, grand commandant seal, Jing and Jiangzhou inspector seals and tallies, halberd insignia.'
translations.idiomatic: I send Yin Xian to return my staff, banners, canopies, court regalia, seals of grand commandant and of the Jing and Jiangzhou inspectorates, and halberd credentials.

sentences.zh: 仰戀天恩，悲酸感結。

translations.literal: Looking up yearning for heaven's grace, grief and sourness feeling knotted.'
translations.idiomatic: I bow to your grace with a breaking heart.

sentences.zh: 以後事付右司馬王愆期，加督護，統領文武。

translations.literal: Entrusted later affairs to right marshal Wang Yanqi, added protector, commanding civil and military.'
translations.idiomatic: He left final dispositions to his right marshal Wang Yanqi as protector over civil and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 侃輿車出臨津就船，明日，薨于樊溪，時年七十六。

translations.literal: Kan by litter went out to Linjin to board boats; the next day died at Fanxi, at the time age seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He was carried in a litter to Linjin to embark and died the next day at Fanxi, aged seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 成帝下詔曰：「故使持節、侍中、太尉、都督荊江雍梁交廣益甯八州諸軍事、荊江二州刺史、長沙郡公經德蘊哲，謀猷弘遠。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng issued an edict saying: 'The late bearer of the staff of authority, palace attendant, grand commandant, area commander for eight provinces' military affairs of Jing, Jiang, Yong, Liang, Jiao, Guang, Yi, and Ning, inspector of Jing and Jiang two provinces, duke of Changsha commandery—classic virtue stored wisdom, plans and schemes vast and far.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng's edict read: "The late commissioner, palace attendant, grand commandant, duke of Changsha—area commander of eight provinces—combined stored virtue with far-reaching counsel."

sentences.zh: 作籓於外，八州肅清；

translations.literal: As fence outside, eight provinces were cleared and solemn;'
translations.idiomatic: On the frontier he kept eight provinces in order;

sentences.zh: 勤王於內，皇家以寧。

translations.literal: diligent to the king within, the imperial house thereby was pacified.'
translations.idiomatic: within the realm he rallied the throne to safety.

sentences.zh: 乃者桓文之勳，伯舅是憑。

translations.literal: In times past Huan and Wen's merit, the elder uncle was relied on.'
translations.idiomatic: Like Huan and Wen of old, the court leaned on this uncle of mine.

sentences.zh: 方賴大猷，俾屏予一人。

translations.literal: Just now relying on the great plan, to screen my lone person.'
translations.idiomatic: I looked to his great strategy to shield me.

sentences.zh: 前進位大司馬，禮秩策命，未及加崇。

translations.literal: Earlier advanced rank grand marshal, ritual order and patent command, not yet reached adding honor.'
translations.idiomatic: His promotion to grand marshal had not yet been fully honored with rites.

sentences.zh: 昊天不吊，奄忽薨殂，朕用震悼於厥心。

translations.literal: High Heaven does not pity; suddenly he passed away; I therefore am shaken in grief in that heart.'
translations.idiomatic: Heaven showed no mercy: he is gone, and my heart is shaken with grief.

sentences.zh: 今遣兼鴻臚追贈大司馬，假蜜章，祠乙太牢。

translations.literal: Now sending concurrent grand master of ceremonies posthumously to grant grand marshal, lent honey-colored seal, sacrifice with grand bull.'
translations.idiomatic: I send the grand master of ceremonies to posthumously confirm him as grand marshal with the honey-colored seal and a great bull offering.

sentences.zh: 魂而有靈，喜茲寵榮。

translations.literal: If the soul has awareness, rejoice in this favor and glory.'
translations.idiomatic: May his aware spirit rejoice in this glory.

sentences.zh: 」又策諡曰桓，祠乙太牢。

translations.literal: Also by patent posthumous title Huan, sacrifice with grand bull.'
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name is to be Huan, with the same grand sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 侃遺令葬國南二十里，故吏刊石立碑畫像于武昌西。

translations.literal: Kan's dying order buried him twenty li south of the state; former clerks carved stone, set up stele and portrait west of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: His testament asked burial twenty li south of the capital; old subordinates carved a stele with his likeness west of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 侃在軍四十一載，雄毅有權，明悟善決斷。

translations.literal: Kan in the army forty-one years, heroic and firm with authority, bright in understanding and good at deciding.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan spent forty-one campaigns under arms, stern, resolute, and decisive.

sentences.zh: 自南陵迄于白帝數千里中，路不拾遺。

translations.literal: From Nanling reaching to White Emperor, in several thousand li, on the road none picked up lost goods.
translations.idiomatic: From Nanling to White Emperor, thousands of li knew no theft on the road.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻之役，庾亮輕進失利。

translations.literal: In the Su Jun campaign, Yu Liang advanced lightly and lost advantage.
translations.idiomatic: During the Su Jun crisis Yu Liang's rash advance had cost the court dearly.

sentences.zh: 亮司馬殷融詣侃謝曰：「將軍為此，非融等所裁。

translations.literal: Liang's marshal Yin Rong went to Kan apologizing, saying: 'The general did this; it is not what Rong and others could cut off.'
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang's marshal Yin Rong apologized to Tao Kan, saying the general's error was beyond their power to stop.

sentences.zh: 」將軍王章至，曰：「章自為之，將軍不知也。

translations.literal: General Wang Zhang arrived, saying: 'Zhang himself did it; the general did not know.'
translations.idiomatic: General Wang Zhang then said he alone was responsible, without Tao Kan's knowledge.

sentences.zh: 」侃曰：「昔殷融為君子，王章為小人；

translations.literal: Kan said: 'Formerly Yin Rong was the gentleman, Wang Zhang the petty man;'
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan observed, "Once I thought Yin Rong the gentleman and Wang Zhang the knave;"

sentences.zh: 今王章為君子，殷融為小人。

translations.literal: now Wang Zhang is the gentleman, Yin Rong the petty man.'
translations.idiomatic: today it is the other way around.

sentences.zh: 」侃性纖密好問，頗類趙廣漢。

translations.literal: Kan's nature was fine-grained and close, fond of asking questions, quite resembling Zhao Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan was meticulous and inquisitive, much in the mold of Zhao Guanghan of Han.

sentences.zh: 嘗課諸營種柳，都尉夏施盜官柳植之於己門。

translations.literal: Once he inspected the camps planting willows; commandant Xia Shi stole official willows and planted them at his own gate.
translations.idiomatic: When he ordered willows planted along the camps, Commandant Xia Shi stole public saplings for his own doorway.

sentences.zh: 侃後見，駐車問曰：「此是武昌西門前柳，何因盜來此種？

translations.literal: Kan afterward saw, halted the cart and asked: 'This is the willow before Wuchang's west gate; why did you steal it to plant here?'
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan later rode past, stopped his carriage, and demanded why the West Gate willows of Wuchang stood at Xia Shi's house.

sentences.zh: 」施惶怖謝罪。

translations.literal: Shi in panic and fear apologized for guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Shi confessed in terror.

sentences.zh: 時武昌號為多士，殷浩、庾翼等皆為佐吏。

translations.literal: At that time Wuchang was called to have many gentlemen; Yin Hao, Yu Yi, and others all were adjutant clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang then teemed with talent—Yin Hao, Yu Yi, and others served on Tao Kan's staff.

sentences.zh: 侃每飲酒有定限，常歡有餘而限已竭，浩等勸更少進，侃淒懷良久曰：「年少曾有酒失，亡親見約，故不敢逾。

translations.literal: Kan whenever drinking wine had a fixed limit; often joy had surplus but the limit was already exhausted; Hao and others urged slightly to advance less; Kan with sorrowful heart long said: 'In youth once had wine fault; deceased parents bound me, therefore dare not exceed.'
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan rationed his wine: merriment often remained when the cup was empty. When Yin Hao pressed him to take a little more, he answered sadly that a youthful drunken shame and his parents' vow kept him from breaking his rule.

sentences.zh: 」議者以武昌北岸有邾城，宜分兵鎮之。

translations.literal: Discussers thought on the north shore of Wuchang there was Zhucheng, ought to divide troops and garrison it.'
translations.idiomatic: Advisers urged him to garrison Zhucheng on the north bank.

sentences.zh: 侃每不答，而言者不已，侃乃渡水獵，引將佐語之曰：「我所以設險而禦寇，正以長江耳。

translations.literal: Kan each time did not answer, yet speakers did not stop; Kan then crossed the water to hunt, led generals and aides and told them: 'That by which I set peril to ward off bandits is precisely the Long River.'
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan ignored the talk until, during a hunt north of the river, he told his officers, "The Yangzi alone is my barrier against raiders."

sentences.zh: 邾城在江北，內無所倚，外接群夷。

translations.literal: Zhucheng is on the Yangzi's north, inward having nothing to lean on, outward connecting the mass of barbarians.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhucheng lies north of the river with no hinterland and opens onto barbarian country.

sentences.zh: 夷中利深，晉人貪利，夷不堪命，必引寇虜，乃致禍之由，非禦寇也。

translations.literal: Among the barbarians profit runs deep; Jin men are greedy for profit; the barbarians cannot bear the command, surely will lead in raiding captives—this is the source of bringing disaster, not warding off bandits.'
translations.idiomatic: Trade there breeds greed on our side and oppression on theirs, inviting invasion rather than preventing it.

sentences.zh: 且吳時此城乃三萬兵守，今縱有兵守之，亦無益於江南。

translations.literal: Moreover in Wu times this city was garrisoned by thirty thousand troops; now even if troops guarded it, it would still not benefit Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Even under Wu thirty thousand men there did little for the south; a garrison today would help Jiangnan even less.

sentences.zh: 若羯虜有可乘之會，此又非所資也。

translations.literal: If Jie captives had an opening to exploit, this would still not be something to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Nor would the fort give us decisive leverage against the Jie horsemen.

sentences.zh: 」後庾亮戍之，果大敗。

translations.literal: Later Yu Liang garrisoned it and met with a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang later held Zhucheng and suffered the crushing defeat Tao Kan had predicted.

sentences.zh: 季年懷止足之分，不與朝權。

translations.literal: In his last years he cherished the sense of knowing enough and did not meddle in court power.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he practiced restraint and stayed clear of court intrigue.

sentences.zh: 未亡一年，欲遜位歸國，佐吏等苦留之。

translations.literal: Within a year of his not having died, he wished to yield his post and return to his fief; adjutants bitterly urged him to stay.
translations.idiomatic: A year before his death he tried to retire to Changsha, but his staff implored him to remain.

sentences.zh: 及疾篤，將歸長沙，軍資器仗牛馬舟船皆有定簿，封印倉庫，自加管鑰以付王愆期，然後登舟，朝野以為美談。

translations.literal: When gravely ill, about to return to Changsha, he recorded every item of army supplies, weapons, oxen, horses, boats, and ships; sealed the storehouses; personally affixed the locks and handed the keys to Wang Yanqi before boarding his boat—court and countryside praised the deed.
translations.idiomatic: As his final illness drove him toward Changsha he inventoried every bolt, blade, ox, and hull, sealed the granaries, locked the treasury himself, and handed the keys to Wang Yanqi before embarking—an exit the whole capital admired.

sentences.zh: 將出府門，顧謂愆期曰：「老子婆娑，正坐諸君輩。

translations.literal: About to leave the prefectural gate, he turned and told Yanqi, 'This old man lingers on only because of you gentlemen.'
translations.idiomatic: At the prefectural gate he turned to Wang Yanqi and said, 'This old fool shuffles on only thanks to the likes of you.'

sentences.zh: 」尚書梅陶與親人曹識書曰：「陶公機神明鑒似魏武，忠順勤勞似孔明，陸抗諸人不能及也。

translations.literal: Secretariat director Mei Tao wrote to kinsman Cao Shi, 'Lord Tao's divine insight resembles Cao Cao of Wei; his loyal diligence resembles Zhuge Liang; Lu Kang and the others cannot match him.'
translations.idiomatic: Mei Tao wrote a kinsman that Tao Kan matched Cao Cao in foresight and Zhuge Liang in loyalty—men like Lu Kang stood below him.

sentences.zh: 」謝安每言「陶公雖用法，而恆得法外意」。

translations.literal: Xie An often remarked that although Lord Tao applied the law, he always grasped the spirit beyond the letter.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An used to say Tao Kan enforced statutes yet always caught their larger meaning.

sentences.zh: 其為世所重如此。

translations.literal: Thus the age esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the world's regard for him.

sentences.zh: 然媵妾數十，家僮千餘，珍奇寶貨富於天府。

translations.literal: Yet he kept dozens of concubines, more than a thousand household slaves, and treasures rivaling the imperial treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he maintained scores of concubines, over a thousand retainers, and wealth that outshone the palace storehouse.

sentences.zh: 或云「侃少時漁于雷澤，網得一織梭，以掛於壁。

translations.literal: Some say that when Kan was young he fished at Lei Marsh, netted a weaver's shuttle, and hung it on the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Legend says that as a youth fishing at Lei Marsh he caught a weaver's shuttle and hung it on his wall.

sentences.zh: 有頃雷雨，自化為龍而去」。

translations.literal: After a time of thunder and rain it transformed itself into a dragon and flew away.
translations.idiomatic: After a storm it turned into a dragon and flew off.

sentences.zh: 又夢生八翼，飛而上天，見天門九重，已登其八，唯一門不得入。

translations.literal: He also dreamed that he grew eight wings, flew up to heaven, saw nine layers of celestial gates, climbed eight of them, but could not enter the ninth.
translations.idiomatic: He dreamed of eight wings, soaring toward nine gates of heaven yet barred from the last.

sentences.zh: 閽者以杖擊之，因隧地，折其左翼。

translations.literal: A gatekeeper struck him with a staff; he fell to earth and broke his left wing.
translations.idiomatic: A gatekeeper struck him down and shattered his left wing.

sentences.zh: 及寤，左腋猶痛。

translations.literal: When he awoke, his left armpit still hurt.
translations.idiomatic: On waking his left side still ached.

sentences.zh: 又嘗如廁，見一人硃衣介幘，斂板曰：「以君長者，故來相報。

translations.literal: Once in a privy he saw a man in vermilion robes and formal cap who, folding his tablet, said, 'Because you are an elder I come to bring word.'
translations.idiomatic: In a latrine vision a red-robed official told him, 'Because you are a man of years I bring tidings.'

sentences.zh: 君後當為公，位至八州都督。

translations.literal: You will become a duke and rise to command eight provinces.
translations.idiomatic: You will rise to duke and command eight provinces.

sentences.zh: 」有善相者師圭謂侃曰：「君左手中指有豎理，當為公。

translations.literal: The physiognomist Shi Gui told Kan, 'A vertical line on your left middle finger marks a dukedom.'
translations.idiomatic: The face-reader Shi Gui said the crease on his left middle finger betokened a dukedom.

sentences.zh: 若徹於上，貴不可言。

translations.literal: If it runs through to the top, honor cannot be spoken.
translations.idiomatic: Were that line to reach the base of the finger, rank would be beyond words.

sentences.zh: 」侃以針決之見血，灑壁而為「公」字，以紙裛，「公」字愈明。

translations.literal: Kan pricked the line with a needle until blood spattered the wall in the shape of the character gong; wrapped in paper, the character grew clearer.
translations.idiomatic: He lanced the line until blood on the wall spelled the character gong (duke); blotting it on paper only sharpened the omen.

sentences.zh: 及都督八州，據上流，握強兵，潛有窺窬之志，每思折翼之祥，自抑而止。

translations.literal: When he commanded eight provinces on the upper Yangzi with a strong army, he secretly harbored designs of usurpation; each time he recalled the omen of the broken wing he checked himself.
translations.idiomatic: Commanding eight provinces with a mighty army, ambition stirred, yet the broken-wing dream curbed him.

sentences.zh: 侃有子十七人，唯洪、瞻、夏、琦、旗、斌、稱、範、岱見舊史，餘者並不顯。

translations.literal: Kan had seventeen sons; only Hong, Zhan, Xia, Qi, Qi (for 旗), Bin, Cheng, Fan, and Dai appear in earlier histories; the rest left no mark.
translations.idiomatic: Of seventeen sons only Hong, Zhan, Xia, Qi, Qi (banner), Bin, Cheng, Fan, and Dai are recorded; the others faded from view.

sentences.zh: 洪，辟丞相掾，早卒。

translations.literal: Hong was summoned as a clerk to the chancellor and died young.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Hong entered the chancellery and died early.

sentences.zh: 瞻，字道真，少有才器，曆廣陵相，廬江、建昌二郡太守，遷散騎常侍、都亭侯。

translations.literal: Zhan, courtesy name Daozhen, showed talent in youth, served as prefect of Guangling and of Lujiang and Jianchang, then as cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and village marquis of Douting.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Zhan, courtesy Daozhen, rose through Guangling and the two prefectures to cavalier attendant-in-ordinary with a Douting marquisate.

sentences.zh: 為蘇峻所害，追贈大鴻臚，諡湣悼世子。

translations.literal: Su Jun killed him; the court posthumously named him grand herald with the epithet Min as heir to the duchy.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun slew him; the throne posthumously made him grand herald with the posthumous name Min as ducal heir.

sentences.zh: 以夏為世子。

translations.literal: Tao Xia was named heir.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Xia succeeded as heir.

sentences.zh: 及送侃喪還長沙，夏與斌及稱各擁兵數千以相圖。

translations.literal: While escorting Kan's funeral to Changsha, Xia, Bin, and Cheng each led thousands of troops against one another.
translations.idiomatic: Escorting the bier to Changsha, Tao Xia, Tao Bin, and Tao Cheng each commanded thousands against one another.

sentences.zh: 既而解散，斌先往長沙，悉取國中器仗財物。

translations.literal: They later dispersed; Bin reached Changsha first and stripped the fief of arms and treasure.
translations.idiomatic: They broke apart, but Tao Bin reached Changsha first and emptied the arsenal and treasury.

sentences.zh: 夏至，殺斌。

translations.literal: When Xia arrived he executed Bin.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao Xia arrived he killed Tao Bin.

sentences.zh: 庾亮上疏曰：「斌雖醜惡，罪在難忍，然王憲有制，骨肉至親，親運刀鋸以刑同體，傷父母之恩，無惻隱之心，應加放黜，以懲暴虐。

translations.literal: Yu Liang memorialized: 'Though Bin's crimes are intolerable, royal law forbids flesh and blood from wielding the executioner's blade against their own kin; banishment would punish the cruelty without severing family grace.'
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang argued that however vile Tao Bin's crime, law forbade a brother from personally executing kin.

sentences.zh: 」亮表未至都，而夏病卒。

translations.literal: Yu Liang's memorial had not reached the capital when Xia died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Before the memorial arrived Tao Xia died of illness.

sentences.zh: 詔復以瞻息弘襲侃爵，仕至光祿勳。

translations.literal: An edict allowed Zhan's son Hong to inherit the duchy; he rose to grand master of splendid carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The throne let Tao Zhan's son Tao Hong inherit the title; he reached grand master of splendid horses.

sentences.zh: 卒，子綽之嗣。

translations.literal: He died; his son Chuozhi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died; Tao Chuozhi inherited.

sentences.zh: 綽之卒，子延壽嗣。

translations.literal: Chuozhi died; his son Yanshou succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Chuozhi was followed by Tao Yanshou.

sentences.zh: 宋受禪，降為吳昌侯，五百戶。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu accepted the abdication the line was demoted to marquis of Wuchang with five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the Song founding the house was reduced to marquis of Wuchang at five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 琦，司空掾。

translations.literal: Qi served as clerk to the minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Qi was a clerk on the minister of works' staff.

sentences.zh: 旗，歷位散騎常侍、郴縣開國伯。

translations.literal: Qi (for 旗) rose to cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and founding baron of Chen county.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Qi (banner graph) became cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and founding baron of Chen.

sentences.zh: 咸和末，為散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: At the end of Xianhe he was attendant cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Xianhe he was attendant cavalier.

sentences.zh: 性甚凶暴。

translations.literal: His nature was very fierce and violent.
translations.idiomatic: He was brutish by nature.

sentences.zh: 卒，子定嗣。

translations.literal: He died; his son Ding succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died; Tao Ding succeeded.

sentences.zh: 卒，子襲之嗣。

translations.literal: Ding died; his son Xizhi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Ding was followed by Tao Xizhi.

sentences.zh: 卒，子謙之嗣。

translations.literal: Xizhi died; his son Qianzhi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Xizhi was followed by Tao Qianzhi.

sentences.zh: 宋受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Song received the abdication the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Liu-Song founding ended the fief.

sentences.zh: 斌，尚書郎。

translations.literal: Tao Bin (a different man from the brother of that name whom Tao Xia slew) was a gentleman of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Another Tao Bin, not the prince murdered in the fraternal feud, served as gentleman of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 稱，東中郎將、南平太守、南蠻校尉、假節。

translations.literal: Cheng was general of the center east, prefect of Nanping, colonel of the southern tribes, with credential staff.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Cheng was general of the center east, Nanping prefect, southern colonel, and bearer of the staff.

sentences.zh: 性虓勇不倫，與諸弟不協。

translations.literal: He was savagely brave beyond the norm and estranged from his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He was violent and quarreled with his brothers.

sentences.zh: 後加建威將軍。

translations.literal: He was later promoted general who establishes might.
translations.idiomatic: He later added the title general who establishes might.

sentences.zh: 咸康五年，庾亮以稱為監江夏隨義陽三郡軍事、南中郎將、江夏相，以本所領二千人自隨。

translations.literal: In Xiankang's fifth year Yu Liang made him supervisor of Jiangxia, Sui, and Yiyang with two thousand household troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth Xiankang year Yu Liang put him over three commanderies with two thousand personal followers.

sentences.zh: 到夏口，輕將二百人下見亮。

translations.literal: At Xiakou he brought only two hundred men to visit Yu Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He arrived at Xiakou with two hundred men to see Yu Liang.

sentences.zh: 亮大會吏佐，責稱前後罪惡，稱拜謝，因罷出。

translations.literal: Yu Liang convened his staff, listed Cheng's crimes; Cheng bowed in apology and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang assembled his clerks, recited Tao Cheng's offenses, took his bow, and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 亮使人於閣外收之，棄市，亮上疏曰：「案稱，大司馬侃之孽子，父亡不居喪位，荒耽於酒，昧利偷榮，擅攝五郡，自謂監軍，輒召王官，聚之軍府。

translations.literal: Yu Liang had guards seize him and executed him in the market, then memorialized that he was Tao Kan's bastard, skipped mourning, drank, embezzled, seized five commanderies, styled himself supervisor, and dragooned courtiers into camp.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang's men seized Tao Cheng for public execution and memorialized his bastardy, skipped mourning, drunkenness, embezzlement, seizure of five commanderies, self-styled supervision, and impressment of officials.

sentences.zh: 故車騎將軍劉弘曾孫安寓居江夏，及將楊恭、趙韶，並以言色有忤，稱放聲當殺，安、恭懼，自赴水而死，韶於獄自盡。

translations.literal: He had threatened Liu An, Yang Gong, and Zhao Shao until two drowned themselves and one hanged in jail.
translations.idiomatic: Liu An, Yang Gong, and Zhao Shao died—two by drowning, one in prison—after his threats.

sentences.zh: 將軍郭開從稱往長沙赴喪，稱疑開附其兄弟，乃反縛懸頭於帆檣，仰而彈之，鼓棹渡江二十餘里，觀者數千，莫不震駭。

translations.literal: When Guo Kai accompanied him to mourning he suspected Guo of favoring his brothers, bound him head-down to the mast, shot him, and rowed twenty li past horrified crowds.
translations.idiomatic: Suspecting Guo Kai of siding with his brothers on the funeral journey, he bound him inverted to the mast, riddled him with arrows, and rowed twenty li past thousands of onlookers.

sentences.zh: 又多藏匿府兵，收坐應死。

translations.literal: He also repeatedly hid imperial troops and deserved death.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly concealed government soldiers and merited execution.

sentences.zh: 臣猶未忍直上，且免其司馬。

translations.literal: Your subject could not bear to memorialize at once and merely removed his marshal.
translations.idiomatic: I could not bring myself to report him immediately and only stripped his marshal.

sentences.zh: 稱肆縱醜言，無所顧忌，要結諸將，欲阻兵構難。

translations.literal: Cheng then slandered freely, courted officers, and plotted mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: He railed without restraint, recruited generals, and plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 諸將惶懼，莫敢酬答，由是奸謀未即髮露。

translations.literal: The generals were too frightened to answer, so the plot stayed hidden awhile.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified officers dared not answer, delaying the plot's exposure.

sentences.zh: 臣以侃勳勞王室，是以依違容掩，故表為南中郎將，與臣相近，思欲有以匡救之。

translations.literal: Because Tao Kan served the throne I temporized and even recommended him as general of the center south nearby, hoping to redeem him.
translations.idiomatic: For Tao Kan's sake I temporized and even posted him nearby as general of the center south to salvage him.

sentences.zh: 而稱豺狼愈甚，發言激切，不忠不孝，莫此之甚。

translations.literal: Instead he grew more wolfish; his speech was more treasonous and unfilial than any I have seen.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he grew fiercer and more disloyal than any man I know.

sentences.zh: 苟利社稷，義有專斷，輒收稱伏法。」

translations.literal: When the altars are at stake a minister may act alone—I have seized Tao Cheng and applied the law.
translations.idiomatic: Where the altars are endangered righteousness allows summary justice—I have arrested Tao Cheng and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 范，最知名，太元初，為光祿勳。

translations.literal: Fan was the most celebrated; early in Taiyuan he became grand master of splendid carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Fan was best known; early in Taiyuan he reached grand master of splendid horses.

sentences.zh: 岱，散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Dai was attendant cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Dai was attendant cavalier.

sentences.zh: 臻字彥遐，有勇略智謀，賜爵當陽亭侯。

translations.literal: Zhen, courtesy Yanxia, was bold and resourceful and enfeoffed village marquis of Dangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Zhen, courtesy Yanxia, was brave and clever with a Dangyang village marquisate.

sentences.zh: 咸和中，為南郡太守、領南蠻校尉、假節。

translations.literal: During Xianhe he was prefect of Nan commandery, colonel of the southern tribes, with credential staff.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianhe he was Nan prefect and southern colonel with the staff of authority.

sentences.zh: 卒官，追贈平南將軍，諡曰肅。

translations.literal: He died in office and was posthumously named general who pacifies the south with the epithet Su.
translations.idiomatic: He died in post and was titled posthumously general who pacifies the south, epithet Su.

sentences.zh: 臻弟輿，果烈善戰，以功累遷武威將軍。

translations.literal: Zhen's younger brother Yu was fierce in battle and rose on merit to general who displays might.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Tao Yu was a fierce fighter promoted to general who displays might.

sentences.zh: 初，賊張奕本中州人，元康中被差西征，遇天下亂，遂留蜀。

translations.literal: The rebel Zhang Yi was a northerner drafted west in Yuankang and stranded in Shu by the wars.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit Zhang Yi was a central-plains man sent west in Yuankang and marooned in Shu.

sentences.zh: 至是，率三百餘家欲就杜弢，為侃所獲。

translations.literal: He now led three hundred households toward Du Tao but Tao Kan captured him.
translations.idiomatic: He led three hundred households toward Du Tao when Tao Kan seized him.

sentences.zh: 諸將請殺其丁壯，取其妻息，輿曰：「此本官兵，數經戰陣，可赦之以為用。

translations.literal: The generals wanted the men killed and families enslaved; Yu said they were government veterans who could still fight if spared.
translations.idiomatic: Officers urged slaughter and enslavement, but Tao Yu said they were imperial troops who could serve if pardoned.

sentences.zh: 」侃赦之，以配輿。

translations.literal: Kan spared them for Yu's command.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan spared them for Tao Yu.

sentences.zh: 及侃與杜弢戰敗，賊以桔槔打沒官軍船艦，軍中失色。

translations.literal: When Tao Kan lost to Du Tao the rebels used well-sweep levers to sink his ships and panicked the camp.
translations.idiomatic: During Tao Kan's defeat the rebels used well-sweep poles to sink government ships and terrified the army.

sentences.zh: 輿率輕舸出其上流以擊之，所向輒克。

translations.literal: Yu took light craft upstream and shattered every attack.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Yu ran light boats upstream and broke each assault.

sentences.zh: 賊又率眾將焚侃輜重，輿又擊破之。

translations.literal: When they tried to burn Tao Kan's baggage train Tao Yu broke them again.
translations.idiomatic: When they tried to burn the baggage Tao Yu defeated them again.

sentences.zh: 自是每戰輒克，賊望見輿軍，相謂曰：「避陶武威。

translations.literal: Thereafter rebels cried to avoid Tao of Wuwei whenever they saw his banners.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the cry was 'Beware Tao of Wuwei!' at sight of his host.

sentences.zh: 」無敢當者。

translations.literal: None dared face him.
translations.idiomatic: None dared oppose him.

sentences.zh: 後與杜弢戰，輿被重創，卒。

translations.literal: He later took mortal wounds fighting Du Tao.
translations.idiomatic: He later died of grave wounds against Du Tao.

sentences.zh: 侃哭之慟，曰：「喪吾家寶！

translations.literal: Kan wept, 'I have lost the jewel of our house!'
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan mourned, 'I have lost the treasure of our house!'

sentences.zh: 」三軍皆為之垂泣。

translations.literal: The whole army wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: The entire host wept.

sentences.zh: 詔贈長沙太守。

translations.literal: The court posthumously named him prefect of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously named him prefect of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：古者明王之建國也，下料疆宇，列為九州，輔相玄功，咨于四嶽。

translations.literal: The historiographers say: When enlightened kings of old founded their states they surveyed the land, carved nine provinces, aided hidden merit, and consulted the four peaks.
translations.idiomatic: The historians write: Ancient kings mapped nine provinces and sought counsel from the four sacred peaks.

sentences.zh: 所以仰希齊政，俯寄宣風。

translations.literal: Thus they aligned policy on high and spread transforming influence below.
translations.idiomatic: They harmonized government above and sent their moral wind below.

sentences.zh: 備連率之儀，威騰閫外；

translations.literal: They invested governors with chained authority whose awe leapt beyond the camp;
translations.idiomatic: Governors bore ritual power that reached beyond the camps;

sentences.zh: 總頒條之務，禮縟區中。

translations.literal: they promulgated statutes and layered rite across the regions.
translations.idiomatic: they issued regulations and thickly spread ritual through the provinces.

sentences.zh: 委稱其才，《甘棠》以之流詠；

translations.literal: When talent matched office the people sang Sweet Pear in praise;
translations.idiomatic: When worth fit post the people sang the Sweet Pear;

sentences.zh: 據非其德，仇餉以是興嗟。

translations.literal: when power lacked virtue even porridge soldiers groaned.
translations.idiomatic: when virtue failed even conscripts sighed.

sentences.zh: 中朝叔世，要荒多阻，分符建節，並紊天綱。

translations.literal: In the Jin court's twilight the frontiers closed; tally after tally tangled heaven's net.
translations.idiomatic: In the dynasty's decline every march was blocked; credentials multiplied until the imperial net snarled.

sentences.zh: 和季以同里之情，申盧綰之契，居方牧之地，振吳起之風。

translations.literal: Liu Heji, sharing a lane with the throne, renewed Lu Wan's bond, ruled a great province, and evoked Wu Qi's spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong, neighbor to the emperor, renewed Lu Wan's friendship, governed a vast region, and brought Wu Qi's vigor.

sentences.zh: 自幽徂荊，亟斂豺狼之跡；

translations.literal: From Youzhou to Jingzhou he stamped out wolves' trails;
translations.idiomatic: From You to Jing he erased predator tracks;

sentences.zh: 舉賢登善，窮掇孔翠之毛。

translations.literal: he raised the worthy and gathered talents like kingfisher plumes.
translations.idiomatic: he lifted the good and gathered talents like peacock feathers.

sentences.zh: 由是吏民畢力，華夷順命，一州清晏，恬波於沸海之中；

translations.literal: Officials and tribes strained until the province lay calm as still water in a boiling sea;
translations.idiomatic: Officers and tribesmen toiled until the province stilled like quiet water amid a raging sea;

sentences.zh: 百城安堵，靜寢於稽天之際。

translations.literal: a hundred cities slept secure though heaven seemed piled upon them.
translations.idiomatic: a hundred cities rested easy though calamity loomed like piled-up heaven.

sentences.zh: 猶獨稱善政，何其寡歟！

translations.literal: Yet men singled him for praise—how rare!
translations.idiomatic: Yet he alone was called a model—how seldom that happens!

sentences.zh: 《易》云「貞固足以幹事」，于征南見之矣。

translations.literal: As the Book of Changes says, firm correctness can accomplish great tasks—this appeared in the southern expeditionary general.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says steadfast duty can carry great tasks—General Tao Kan proved it.

sentences.zh: 士行望非世族，俗異諸華，拔萃陬落之間，比肩髦俊之列，超居外相，宏總上流。

translations.literal: Shixing was no great clan and differed from central-plain ways; he rose from a remote corner to rank with the finest, leapt to outer minister, and broadly commanded the upper Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan, no aristocrat and an outsider to Huaxia custom, rose from obscurity among the elite to command the whole middle Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 布澤懷邊，則嚴城靜柝；

translations.literal: His kindness along the borders stilled every watchtower;
translations.idiomatic: His grace on the frontier hushed every night drum;

sentences.zh: 釋位匡主，則淪鼎再寧。

translations.literal: when he set aside office to save his ruler the sunk cauldron twice found peace.
translations.idiomatic: when he laid down power to aid the throne the dynasty twice recovered.

sentences.zh: 元規以戚裏之崇，挹其膺而下拜；

translations.literal: Yu Liang, kin to the throne, bowed from the heart;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang of the imperial clan bowed low;

sentences.zh: 茂弘以保衡之貴，服其言而動色。

translations.literal: Wang Dao, guardian minister, heard his words and blanched.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao, pillar of state, listened and changed color.

sentences.zh: 望隆分陝，理則宜然。

translations.literal: His stature matched guardians of the western realm—fitting indeed by every principle.
translations.idiomatic: His eminence rivaled the old lords of the western march—only right.

sentences.zh: 至於時屬雲屯，富逾天府，潛有包藏之志，顧思折翼之祥，悖矣！

translations.literal: As for the time belonging to clouds massed, wealth exceeding the heavenly treasury, secretly having the will to embrace and conceal, yet turning to think of the auspice of the broken wing—contradictory!
translations.idiomatic: To amass power and riches rivaling the throne yet still heed the omen of a broken wing shows how even towering strength can contradict itself.

sentences.zh: 夫子曰「人無求備」，斯言之信，於是有征。

translations.literal: The Master said, 'In people do not seek completeness'; the trustworthiness of this saying, in this there is proof.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said we should not demand perfection of any man—and here is the proof.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：和季承恩，建旟南服。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: Heji received grace, raised banners in the southern garments.
translations.idiomatic: Eulogy: Liu Heji bore imperial favor and raised the standard in the southern lands.

sentences.zh: 威靜荊塞，化揚江澳。

translations.literal: Awe stilled the Jing passes; transformation raised on the Yangtze's bays.
translations.idiomatic: His authority stilled the Jing garrisons; his rule spread virtue along the great river.

sentences.zh: 戮力天朝，匪忘忠肅。

translations.literal: Joined strength to the heavenly court, did not forget loyal solemnity.
translations.idiomatic: He strained every nerve for the dynasty and never slackened in loyal duty.

sentences.zh: 長沙勤王，擁旆戎場。

translations.literal: Changsha labored for the king, grasped pennants on the battleground.
translations.idiomatic: The lord of Changsha rallied to the throne and bore his banner through every campaign.

sentences.zh: 任隆三事，功宣一匡。

translations.literal: Trust rose to the three tasks; merit proclaimed one correction.
translations.idiomatic: He was trusted with the highest offices and his service set the realm upright.

sentences.zh: 繄賴之重，匪伊舟航。

translations.literal: The weight of reliance—was it only boats and ships?
translations.idiomatic: The court leaned on him for far more than fleets and convoys alone.
